In the cool season, he fasts at the armpit of the axle. 4.1.1.2.
Those [plants] come forth in the spring.

4.1.1.3. On the full moon day of the month of Phalguna, he curdles the remains of the *agnihotra* offering and sets it aside for the purpose of curdling the sacrificial oblation (*havirātañcana*). 4.1.1.4.
Having gone outside, he cuts a branch of the *palāśa* tree with the formula: "For food thee! For strength thee! (TS 1.1.1.a).

4.1.1.5. Having gone there, he drives away the calves with the formula: “You are the winds; you are the approaching ones. 4.1.1.6. He consecrates the cows with the formula: “May the god Savitṛ impel you for the most excellent rite; swell, O inviolable ones, as portions rich in vigor and rich in milk for all the gods. Thus it is accomplished.
4.1.1.7. Having taken the knife with the formula, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ," he goes out toward the edge of the thicket.
4.1.1.8. He cuts the shoots that they are about to consume.
4.1.1.9. Having filled the *prastara* [bunch], he places it down.
4.1.1.10. He cuts the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). 4.1.1.11.
There he binds it in three parts. 4.1.1.12.
He binds the *prastara* bundle together with one of them.
4.1.1.13. Then he girds himself once again. 4.1.1.14. The other [ritual acts] are well-known; he cuts the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
4.1.1.15. While bringing the materials for the *ārambhaṇīyā* sacrifice, he goes forth.

4.1.1.16. Having arranged the sacrificial implements and having carried forward the waters, he offers the *ārambhaṇīyā* sacrifice: a cake on twelve potsherds for Prajāpati, a pap for the Seasons, a cake on twelve potsherds for Vaiśvānara, a pap for Parjanya, and a cake on three potsherds for Viṣṇu.
4.1.1.17. Once the oblation has been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* verses and the *pṛśni* verses.
4.1.1.18. When [the oblation] has been placed near [the fire], he recites the *apānagraha* verses, the *pṛśni* verses, and the *daśahotṛ* formula.
4.1.1.19. For that [offering], the two *vārtraghna* butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*) are used.
4.1.1.20. Saying, “Recite for Prajāpati,” he speaks while spreading [the underlayer] and cutting [the portion].
4.1.1.21. He recites the invitatory verse: “O Prajāpati, none other than you possesses these.
4.1.1.22. He offers with the offering verse: “He knows. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the oblation.
4.1.1.23. Saying, “Recite for the seasons,” he says this while spreading [the underlayer] and cutting [the portions].
4.1.1.24. He recites: “Summer, winter. 4.1.1.25. He sacrifices with the formula, “To the year,” and offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.

4.1.1.26. "Recite for Vaiśvānara," he says, while spreading [the base] and cutting [the portion]. 4.1.1.27. He recites: "For Vaiśvānara of broad power... (Ṛgveda 3.3.1), ending with: "...he has not harmed the eternal laws" (*vivo ratnā vidhanta dharuṇeṣu gātave agnir hi devāṃ amṛto duvasyaty athā dharmāṇi sanatāna dūduṣat*).

4.1.1.28. He sacrifices with the verse, “O Agni, you... (RV 7.13.2): “With your flame, O you who shine intensely, at your birth you filled both worlds; O Vaiśvānara Jātavedas, by your greatness you released the gods from the curse.
4.1.1.29. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering. 4.1.1.30. Saying, “Recite for Parjanya,” he spreads the underlayer and cuts the portions.

4.1.1.32. He offers with the verse, "Speak forth to the powerful one" (*acchā vada tavasaṃ*); [he recites]: "Praise Parjanya with songs and hymns; win him over with homage; thundering forth... (*gīrbhir ukthaiḥ stuhi parjanyaṃ namasā vivāsa abhikrandan*).
"Let the bellowing bull, rich in vigor, bestow seed as a germ within the plants.
(VS 27.35) 4.1.1.33. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering. 4.1.1.34. While spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portions], he says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Viṣṇu."
4.1.1.35. He recites [the verse]: "Viṣṇu strode through this. 4.1.1.36.

He offers the oblation with [the verse]: "May I attain that beloved station of his... and "...wherein the men devoted to the gods rejoice; where they drink from the fountain of the wide-striding one, exulting in the praise-hymn of Viṣṇu at the highest step of the sweet [soma].
4.1.1.37. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
4.1.1.38. Its sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is a draft ox (*anaḍvān*), a heifer, a bull, or a cow that is either barren or short of stature.
4.1.1.39. Following the continuity, he offers the oblation for the Hotṛ priest.
4.1.1.40. The rite is successfully accomplished; the *ārambhaṇīyeṣṭi* (inaugural sacrifice) is concluded.
4.1.1.41. With the vessels washed, he awaits the cows as they approach at evening.

4.1.1.42. After offering the *agnihotra* with the verse, "These come, milking the honey-sweet [milk]," he milks the *sānnāyya* with the formula, "May she yield much milk, the oblation for all the gods.
4.1.1.43. With the formula, "May the Viśve Devas, the Vaiśvānaras, mix you," he places it down.
4.1.1.44. With the words, “I curdle you with Soma as the portion of all the gods,” he curdles the oblation by means of the curdling agent (ātañcana).
4.1.1.45. With the words, “Thou art invincible; for all the gods, thee,” he covers it with a vessel containing water.
4.1.1.46. With the words, “O Agni, protect the oblation,” he places it where he considers it to be secure.

4.1.1.47. In this very manner, having offered the morning *agnihotra*, he causes the *sānnāyya* milk to be milked. 4.1.1.48. Herein, he does not wait for the [milk to cool]; he does not heat it; he does not pour water back into it; and he does not anoint it, up to the point of washing. 4.1.1.49. Having arranged the sacrificial implements (*yajñāyudha*) and having led forward the ritual waters (*praṇītā-apaḥ*), he offers the oblation for the *vaiśvadeva*.
4.1.1.50. An offering to Agni on eight potsherds.

He offers an oblation to Agni on eight potsherds, a *caru* to Soma, a cake on twelve potsherds to Savitṛ, a *caru* to Sarasvatī, a *caru* to Pūṣan, a cake on seven potsherds to the Maruts, *āmikṣā* to the Viśve Devas, and a cake on one potsherd to Dyāvāpṛthivī.
4.1.2.2. Once the oblation has been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* verses and the *pṛśni* verses.

4.1.2.3. Having released his speech with the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviskṛt*), he offers the *pañcahotṛ* formula into the *āhavanīya* fire with [clarified butter] taken up four times.
4.1.2.4. The oblations are cooked; he prepares the *āmikṣā* curd-mixture while [the milk] is boiling.
4.1.2.5. Either he pours curds into the boiled milk, or he pours the boiled milk into the curds.
4.1.2.6. When the oblations have been boiled, he performs the *stambayajus* rite.
4.1.2.7. He encloses the altar and mutters the *karaṇa* formula.
4.1.2.8. Once the [Soma] has been pressed, he performs the subsequent tracing of the altar; he mutters the *karaṇa* formula.

4.1.2.9. Having stirred [the water] and having propped [the ladle], he issues the command: "Set down the sprinkling waters; gird the wife; come forth with the clarified butter! Set down the fuel and the sacrificial grass; cleanse the dipping-spoon and the offering-ladles; gird the wife; come forth with the clarified butter! Bring the curds for the speckled butter; come, O sacrificer! 4.1.2.10. They do these things.
4.1.2.11. Having wiped the *sruk* and the *sruc*s, he takes the clarified butter (*ājya*) and the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*).
4.1.2.12. He sprinkles the fuel (*idhma*) and the sacrificial grass (*barhis*); he sprinkles the altar (*vedi*); he sprinkles what has been placed [on it]. 4.1.2.13.
Having poured out the water, he takes the *prastara* [bunch of grass]; he spreads the sacrificial grass.
4.1.2.14. Having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
4.1.2.15. He places two fuel-sticks (*samidh*) on the fire. 4.1.2.16. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing sticks, he yokes the fire.

4.1.2.17. Having come back, he places [the *āmikṣā*] crosswise; he places the *prastara* on the two crosswise [straw-bundles], the *juhū* on the *prastara*, and they adorn the other two [spoons] with sacrificial grass (*barhis*).

4.1.2.18. He places the oblations one after another. Having spread an underlayer of ghee and poured ghee over them, he draws out the *āmikṣā* which has been spread with an underlayer and poured over with ghee.
4.1.2.19 {Not in C}. Having sprinkled [the butter] over the horse, he sets it down.
4.1.2.20. Having sprinkled [butter] over the sacrificial oblations, they bring them forward when they have been set down.
4.1.2.21. When they have been set down, he recites the formulas for the *apānagraha* cups and the *pṛśni* cups.

4.1.2.22. Having wiped [the ladle] together with the mantra, "They have sat down firmly; that which is mine, O Agni" (cf. MS 1.1.12:8.3; KS 1.11:6; VS 2.6), he recites the Pañcahotṛ formula. 4.1.2.23.
They proceed with the fire produced by friction (*nirmanthya*). 4.1.2.24. He pronounces the invitatory verses for the fire being kindled; he recites seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses.

4.1.2.25. While invoking [the gods], he also invokes the *vājina*s (the swift ones). 4.1.2.26. After the *sāmidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* ladle, he says to the *āgnīdh*: "O *āgnīdh*, cleanse the fire three times each. 4.1.2.27. Having stepped across without letting the two offering-ladles (*sruc*) touch each other, and having anointed the *dhruvā* ladle, he sets it down and chooses the *pravara* (the ancestral invocation).
4.1.2.27. The Hotṛ sits down, having been impelled. 4.1.2.28. He takes up the two offering-spoons; he performs nine fore-offerings (prayāja). 4.1.2.29.

[The Adhvaryu] says, "Oṃ, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to announce! [The Āgnīdhra] says, "Oṃ, cause to announce! [The Adhvaryu says,] "Recite the offering-verse for the fuel-sticks (samidh)," and [then], "Recite! Recite! for each subsequent one.
4.1.2.29. At the fourth [offering], having poured in half; at the eighth, pour in all [the butter]. 4.1.2.30.
He performs the fore-offerings (*prayāja*) entirely from the *upabhṛt* [ladle]. 4.1.2.31.

Having performed the fore-offerings and stepped across, he bastes the *dhruvā* [ladle], and then the oblations in order, with the clotted butter (*pṛṣadājya*) last; he does not [baste] the *upabhṛt*, for it remains empty.
4.1.2.32. He offers the two *ājyabhāga* portions. The two *ājyabhāga* offerings belong to Vṛtrahan. [x4] 4.1.2.E. "Recite for Agni," he says, while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portion].
4.1.3 [N1,39b4; C47;(M111;T1,129)]{A misspelling of leaves in N1: N1 ends 39b at "iti ya" (4.1.3.14), while 40a begins at 4.3.1.20. Several leaves must be missing in N1 in between.}
4.1.3.1. He says, "Recite for Agni," while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portion]. 4.1.3.2.

He recites [the invitatory verse], "Agni is the head (4.1.11c, p.=TB3.7.5.1)," and he offers [the oblation], "Bhuvaḥ (4.1.11d, p.=TB3.7.5.1). At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 4.1.3.3. He says, "Recite for Soma," while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portion].

4.1.3.4. He recites, “O Soma, [protect] us from all sides” (4.1.11e = 2.3.14e); he offers with the verse, “Those abodes which are yours” (4.1.11f = 2.3.14f); and when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the oblation. 4.1.3.5.

Saying, “Recite for Śavitṛ,” he speaks while spreading the underlayer and cutting the portion. 4.1.3.6. He recites, “That most excellent splendor of Savitṛ” (4.1.11g); he offers with the verse, “Through lack of thought” (4.1.11h); and when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the oblation.

4.1.3.7. "Recite for Sarasvatī," he says, while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portion]. 4.1.3.8. He recites after [the invitatory verse]: "The impeller of true blessings... (ibid. i); he offers the oblation with [the offering verse]: "...the daughter of lightning... (ibid. k). When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering. 4.1.3.9. "Recite for Pūṣan," he says, while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portion]. "Recite for Pūṣan," he says, while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portion].

4.1.3.10. He recites: “May Pūṣan follow our cows” (ibid.); he offers with the formula: “One [portion] of yours is bright” (ibid.). At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. He recites: “May Pūṣan follow our cows” (ibid.); he offers with the formula: “One [portion] of yours is bright” (ibid.). At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 4.1.3.11. “Recite for the Maruts,” he says, while spreading [the base of clarified butter] and cutting [the portions].

4.1.3.12. He recites [the verse]: "O Maruts, when indeed [you come] from heaven... (RV 1.5.11p = 2.1.11c = 2.3.14r). He offers the oblation at the *vaṣaṭ*-call after he has sacrificed with [the formula]: "...as much as [your] protection" (*yāvac charma*) (RV 1.5.11q = 2.1.11d = 2.3.14s). 4.1.3.13. [The Adhvaryu] says, "Recite for the Viśve Devas," while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portions].

4.1.3.14. He recites, “O All-Gods, increasers of Truth” (2.4.14q = 4.1.11.4p), and he offers the oblation with, “O All-Gods, hear this invocation” (2.4.14r = 4.1.11q). When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering.
4.1.3.15. “Recite for Heaven and Earth,” he says.
4.1.3.16. Spreading [the butter] underneath, he pours [the butter] over [the oblation].

4.1.3.17. While placing that cake on a single potsherd (*ekakapāla*), he recites, "O Heaven and Earth, this... (4.1.11r), and he offers with the verse, "Forward, O first-born... (4.1.11s). At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the oblation. 4.1.3.18. He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt," while spreading [ghee] and cutting [the portions].
4.1.3.19. He cuts off a portion once from the northern half of each of all the sacrificial offerings (*havir*).

4.1.3.20. Having taken a portion from the single potsherd from the *āśaya* vessel, he pours clarified butter over it twice; he does not anoint it back. 4.1.3.21. The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *gāyatrī* metre. 4.1.3.22. He recites the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*): "Awaken Agni with a hymn... (4.1.11t); he performs the offering (*yajati*) with the formula "...the bearer of oblations" (4.1.11u). At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the libation.
4.1.3.23. Having stepped across and placed the two offering spoons in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion.
4.1.3.24. Having touched water, he cuts off the *iḍā* portion.
4.1.3.25. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places [the portions] for the *agnīdh*.
4.1.3.26. They consume [the portions], they sprinkle themselves for purification, and they carry [the remains] around.
4.1.3.27. When the *prāśitra* portion has been consumed by the *brahmán*, having thrown the sacrificer’s share into the *caru* vessel, they remove it from the fire.
4.1.3.28. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite over the sacrificial oblations (*havīṃṣi*) at the *anvāhārya* rice mess.
4.1.3.29. They set down the *vājina* (the whey).
4.1.3.30. Following the continuity, he offers eight *viṣṭambha-anvāroha* oblations with the formula: “To *asava* svāhā! (4.1.4) [K4,26b11–; M112;
T1,131] (N1 missing)

4.1.4.11. “To Asu, svāhā! To Vasu, svāhā! To Vibhu, svāhā! To Vivasvat, svāhā!”—these are the *viṣṭambhas*. “To Madhu, svāhā! To Mādhava, svāhā! To Śukra, svāhā! To Śuci, svāhā!”—these are the *anvārohas*. 4.1.4.2. Having said, “Come, O sacrificer,” and while the sacrificer has taken hold of him, the Hotṛ offers the ninth oblation.
4.1.4.3. Saying, "O Brahman, we shall set forth," he performs nine after-offerings (*anuyāja*) with speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*).

4.1.4.4. Having returned, he separates the two offering-spoons (*sruk*) with two verses addressed to Vāyu; with the *śaṃyu* formula, he strews together the sacrificial grass-bundle (*prastara*) and the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
4.1.4.5. Having touched water, while pouring [the remains] into the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) from the spoon that has not been smeared with clarified butter, he brings in the whey (*vājina*).
4.1.4.6. Saying, “Recite for the Vājins,” the Adhvaryu, rising up, says [this].
4.1.4.7. He recites: “In every contest, O Vājins, protect us! 4.1.4.8. He performs the sacrifice with: “May the Vājins be gracious to us!”
4.1.4.9. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers; he performs the secondary *vaṣaṭ* call for this [oblation] while holding the ladle upright. 4.1.4.10.
With the words, "O Agni, enjoy the *vājina*," he offers to the quarters.
4.1.4.11. He leaves over a portion for the *bhakṣa*.
4.1.4.122. Its consumption [is prescribed].

4.1.4.13. With the verse: "I have consumed the sweet draught of the wise one, the well-intentioned, the bestower of wide space; him whom all the gods and mortals follow as they move along, calling him honey"—the Hotṛ consumes first, then the Adhvaryu, then the Brahman, then the Āgnīdhra, and then the Sacrificer.
4.1.4.14. They consume [the portions] with their breaths; for the sacrificer, the consumption is direct. 4.1.4.15. Having gone beyond, they perform the *saṃyājana* offerings for the wives. 4.1.4.16.

Having offered the *phalīkaraṇa* oblation and having come forward to the east, he offers three *samiṣṭayajus* oblations: "O Sacrifice, go to the Sacrifice; go to the Lord of the Sacrifice; go to your own womb, svāhā!"

"O Lord of Sacrifice, may this sacrifice of yours, accompanied by hymns and rich in heroes, be consecrated with Svāhā!"—having offered thus with the *sruva*-ladle and having replenished the *dhruvā* vessel, he offers with the *sruc* (or *sruva*) ladle [using the mantra]: "O gods who know the way... (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 3.2.5.1–k). Having found the way, go on the way, O Lord of Mind; O God, place this sacrifice of ours among the gods, Svāhā! To Speech, Svāhā! To Wind, place it! Thus, at the conclusion of the rite, he turns back from the oblation.

4.1.4.18. These materials are prepared for him: a three-striped porcupine quill, a razor of red metal, a bronze vessel, gold, arrows, and a bow. He spreads the arrows upon the sacrificer’s seat. 4.1.4.19.
The sacrificer sits down upon them, having turned toward the east and made a lap; having placed the gold into the bronze vessel, he pours water into it.
4.1.4.20. At the end of those [verses], having grasped them with a three-spined porcupine quill, he shaves [the hair] with an iron razor.

4.1.4.21. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: “*Ṛta* indeed is the Supreme Lord (*parameṣṭhin*)”; “Nothing whatsoever transgresses *ṛta*; upon *ṛta* the ocean is established; by *ṛta* the earth is made firm. The *uṣṇihā* has stepped upon the head; the *uṣṇihā* has stepped upon the head. Agni Vaiśvānara with his sharp flame—[thus C].”

“With splendor, with *ṛta*, I turn you back; with truth, I turn you around; with auspiciousness, I turn you toward me. That is *ṛta*, that is truth, that is the vow; may I be able to accomplish it, may I be able through it, may I prosper through it.
(4.1.4.22) He shaves first in front, then on the south side, then on the west, then on the north, and then in the middle.
(4.1.4.23) Following the conclusion of the oblation, he performs the sacrifice with the well-known full-moon oblation (*paurṇamāsa-havis*).

4.1.4.24. He observes the *devavrata* vows: he does not speak untruth, he does not eat meat, he does not approach a woman, they do not wash his garment with lye, he sleeps on the ground, he drinks from vessels that are not made of clay, he does not consume the leavings of a *śūdra*, and he washes his own feet himself. "He should eat only what is given as alms," says the manual for the performer of the *Cāturmāsya* sacrifices.
Thus ends the first section. 4.2.1. Now, therefore, the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings.

4.2.1.2. Their equipment consists of four cauldrons, the two sets of sacrificial implements, two bundles of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), four fuel-sticks (*idhma*), two altars—the northern altar (*uttaravedi*) and [the other]—rice and barley, reed-grass, a winnowing basket, *śamī* leaves, flour of *karīra* fruit, and the wool of a ewe and a ram.
4.2.1.33. On the full moon day of the month of Āṣāḍha, having curdled the remains of the *agnihotra* offering, he sets it aside for the curdling of the sacrificial oblation (*havirātañcana*).

4.2.1.44. Having gone out further, he cuts off a branch of the *palāśa* tree with the formula: "For food thee! For strength thee! 4.2.1.5. Having returned by that same way, he drives away the calves with the formula: "Ye are the winds; ye are the approachers."

4.2.1.65. He consecrates the cows with the mantra: “May the god Savitṛ impel you. [The formula continues: “O inviolable ones, for the most excellent Maruts and Varuṇa, [I offer] you, who are full of vigor and full of milk, as a portion. This is established. 4.2.1.7.
Having taken up a flint-knife with the words, “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ,” he goes out toward the half of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) that lies beyond; this is established.
4.2.1.8. He cuts two bundles of sacrificial grass (*barhis*): one with a *yajus* formula and the other silently.
4.2.1.9. Having brought them, he goes back. 4.2.1.10.
At evening, with cleansed vessels, he waits for the cows as they return; at morning, [he waits] with cleansed vessels. These [cows] come toward him.

4.2.1.11. Having offered the Agnihotra with the verse, "Yielding sweetness," he causes the *sannāyya* (curdled milk) to be milked with the formula, "Yield much for the Maruts; [yield] the oblation for Varuṇa. 4.2.1.12. With the formula, "May the Maruts and Varuṇa mix you," he places that [mixture] down after it has been moistened. 4.2.1.13. With the formula, "I mix the portion of the Maruts and of Varuṇa for you two with Soma," he mixes the oblation by means of the *ātañcana* (sour-milk mixture).
4.2.1.14. With the formula, “You two belong to the Maruts; you are for the Maruts and for Varuṇa,” he covers [the vessels] with two vessels containing water.
4.2.1.15. With the formula, “O Agni, protect the oblation,” he places them where he considers them to be secure.
4.2.1.16. In this very same way, having offered the morning *agnihotra*, he causes the *sānnāyya* to be milked.

4.2.1.17. Herein, he does not wait; he does not illuminate [the water]; he does not bring back the water. Having washed the sacrificial implements up to the end, having set them down, and having brought forward the water, the altars are prepared to the east of the Āhavanīya fire; he does not anoint [them] at the end of the washing.

4.2.1.18. To the east of the Āhavanīya fire, within the altar (antarvedi), two [mounds] are prepared, separated by a distance of one span (pṛthamātra) and not joined together; on the northern [side], there is the Uttaravedi. 4.2.1.19. He takes the two *stambayajus* portions from them: the Adhvaryu from the northern [mound], and the Pratiprasthātṛ from the southern. 4.2.1.20. They take up their respective wooden spades (*sphya*) separately. The ritual action for the Pratiprasthātṛ is performed silently.
4.2.1.216. “Whatever the *adhvaryu* does, that the *pratiprasthātṛ* does”—this is the Brāhmaṇa (TB 1.6.5.1–2).
4.2.1.22. Having enclosed the two altars (*vedī*), he mutters the formula for the performance.
4.2.1.23. ... “Take it!”—he scatters the earth for the *uttaravedi*.

4.2.1.24 {Not in T1}. "Kindle the fuel-wood! Prepare the supporting ladles! 4.2.1.25. {Having issued the command, "The wooden sword and the water-vessel!", he carries them forward to the Āgnīdhra fire.} They carry the two fires forward according to the procedure for the fire. 4.2.1.26. The ritual action is successfully completed through the *atimukti* offerings.
4.2.1.27. Having offered the *atimukti* oblations, having arranged the sacrificial implements, and having brought forward the water, he offers the *varuṇapraghāsa* oblations.

4.2.1.28. He offers an oblation on eight potsherds to Agni; a pap to Soma; a cake on twelve potsherds to Savitṛ; a pap to Sarasvatī; a pap to Pūṣan; a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra and Agni; a curd-mixture (*āmikṣā*) for the Maruts; a curd-mixture for Varuṇa; and a cake on one potsherd to Ka. 4.2.1.29. Once the offerings have been set out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.
4.2.1.30. Having released his speech with the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*), he offers the *pañcahotṛ* formula with four portions of ghee into the Āhavanīya fire.
4.2.1.31. He prepares bowls of groat-mash (*karambhapātra*) from barley grains that have been parched and ground, one for each person.
4.2.1.32. He makes one extra bowl; he prepares a ram and a ewe. 4.2.1.33. He attaches the wool of the ram to the ewe.
4.2.1.34. They place the wool of a ewe on a ram and a winnowing basket made of reeds.

4.2.1.35. The oblations are cooked; they prepare the *āmikṣā* curds. 4.2.1.36. Or, when the two [milk products] have been boiled, they pour curdled milk (*dadhi*) into them; or, when the two [portions of] curdled milk have been boiled, [they pour the boiled milk into them].
4.2.1.37. When the oblations have been cooked, they both take up their wooden spades (sphya), saying: "O Brahman, we two shall perform the two subsequent enclosures.
4.2.1.38. Once the waters have been led forth, they perform the two subsequent enclosures.

4.2.1.39. Having leveled [the ground] and propped it up, he issues the command: "Set down the sprinkling waters; place the fuel and the sacrificial grass nearby; cleanse the *sruva* and the *sruk* ladles; gird the wife; come forth with the clarified butter; bring the curds for the clotted butter (*pṛṣadājya*); come, O sacrificer!"—they perform these actions as prescribed in 4.2.1.36.

4.2.1.37. Having wiped the two *sruva* ladles and the *sruc* spoons, the Adhvaryu takes the clarified butter (*ājya*) portions; the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the portions of speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*). In the established manner, the Pratiprasthātṛ silently sprinkles the fuel-sticks (*idhma*) and the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), and sprinkles the altar (*vedi*). Having sprinkled them and poured out the remaining water, they take up the *prastara* bundles and spread the sacrificial grass. Having stepped forward toward the east, they lay down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), they put on the fuel-sticks (*samidh*) and yoke the two fires.

Having returned, they place the two *tiraścīna* [sticks] upon the two *tiraścī* [enclosing sticks], the two *prastara* [bundles] upon the two *prastara* [sticks], and the other two *barhis* [blades] upon the two *sruk* [ladles].
While adorning them, they arrange the sacrificial oblations (*havir*) in due order.
4.2.1.40. When the *āmikṣā* has been spread with flour and sprinkled with ghee, he removes a portion for the Maruts and places a ram upon it.
He places a ram upon the offering for the Maruts and a ewe upon the offering for Varuṇa.

4.2.2.2. With those two [ladles], they scatter *śamī* leaves and *karīra*-flour; having covered one [ladle] with a hundred axe-heads, he likewise covers the other and places the *vājina* (curd-mixture) upon it.
4.2.2.3. Having sprinkled [the oblations] with clarified butter, they bring the sacrificial offerings.

4.2.2.4. The Adhvaryu places the offerings for Indra and Agni on the northern altar, the Pratiprasthātṛ places the offering for the Maruts on the southern altar, and the Adhvaryu places the offerings for Varuṇa and Ka on the northern altar.
4.2.2.5. When [the rite] is near its conclusion, he recites the *apānagrahas* and the *pṛśni* verses.

4.2.2.6. Having touched [the fire] while reciting, "The steadfast ones have settled; that which is mine, O Agni... (*yan me agne*), he recites the *pañcahotṛ* formula. 4.2.2.7. He proceeds with the fire produced by friction and recites the invitatory verse for the fire being kindled.
4.2.2.8. He recites seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses. 4.2.2.9. While invoking [the gods], he also invokes the *vājins*.
4.2.2.10. When the *sāmidhenīs* have been recited, they both offer the two libations (*āghāra*) with the two *sruva* spoons.
4.2.2.11. Then [the Adhvaryu] says to the Āgnīdhra: "O Āgnīdhra, cleanse the fires three times each. 4.2.2.12.
The northern fire has been cleansed, while the southern one remains uncleansed.
4.2.2.13. Then, having run (or gone) [to the wife], the Pratiprasthātṛ asks the wife: "Wife, how many paramours do you have? She should say, "So many," as many as there actually are.
4.2.2.14. If they were not to exist—if one were to say, "They do not exist"—[then the following would apply].
4.2.2.15. If they were innumerable, one should take up a handful of dust, saying, "These are fewer than those.
4.2.2.16. If she does not name her living paramour, she obstructs a dear kinsman; she should point him out, saying, "This man is my paramour."
4.2.2.17. “May Varuṇa seize him whom [the sacrificer] hates; let him seize him!”—thus he meditates upon the one whom the sacrificer hates.

4.2.2.18. With the words, “We invoke the *praghāsas*; we invoke the *praghāsas*,” (TS 1.8.3b), the *pratiprasthātṛ* leads the wife to the south of the *anvāhāryapacana* fire, carrying the vessels of *karambha* in a winnowing-basket made of *aiṣīka* grass. (TS 1.8.3b: “O Maruts, at the sacrifice...”)
"O Maruts, who carry the sacrifice, being of one accord with the *karambha*—being of one accord!
(1.8.3.b). As they approach, the sacrificer, having risen toward the southern fire and having paid homage to it, takes the *karambha* vessels from it.

4.2.2.207. Having placed [the cup] upon his head, standing in front and facing west, he recites the *puro’nuvākyā*: "{*Thus T1, C: mo Sma[TS: Su] Na indra .. l.c. c .. gīr*}, *mo Sū Na indra vandate gīr*. [E112-3, n.569, Cal Ī152,10] 4.2.2.21. "Both [recite] the *yājyā*," so says the Brāhmaṇa.

4.2.2.22. With the words, “Whatever in the village, whatever in the forest” (TS 1.8.3d), the Pratiprasthātṛ makes the wife recite: “Whatever in the assembly... [omitted] ...thou art the expiation, svāhā!”—that is, “Whatever in the assembly, if there be anything [of that], thou art the expiation, svāhā!
[cf. Vājasaneyins, E117]. 4.2.2.23. He throws away the winnowing basket made of *aiṣīka* grass with the formula: “They have performed the cooking; we perform the rite.”

4.2.2.24. With the formula, “They have performed the work, the work-doers” (TS 1.8.3e), the Pratiprasthātṛ leads [the butter]; with the formula, “Together with speech, O bounteous ones, bringing bliss” (TS 1.8.3f).
4.2.2.25. The wife returns; the sacrificer sits down to the south. The Agnīdh cleanses the southern fire.

4.2.2.26. They pour the two subsequent *āghāra* libations with the *sruk* ladles, either touching them [together] or not touching the *sruk*s; having stepped across [the altar], having anointed the *sruva* spoons and set them down, he chooses the *pravara*.
4.2.2.27. The *hotṛ* sits down.
4.2.2.28. Being impelled, they take up the two *sruk* ladles.
4.2.2.29. He performs the *prayāja* offerings. [The Adhvaryu] says: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard!
(Cf. E118). 4.2.2.30. "Recite the offering prayer for the *samidh*s. [He says] "Recite! Recite! 4.2.2.31.
Having poured half [of the butter] into the *upabhṛt* at the fourth [offering], he pours all [the remainder] into it at the eighth; the Adhvaryu leaves a residue in the *upabhṛt*.
4.2.2.32. Having performed the *prayāja* offerings for the subsequent sacrifices (*anūyāja*), the *pratiprasthātṛ* steps across and pours clarified butter over the *dhruva* ladle.

4.2.2.33. From the *aindrāgna* [offering], the *adhvaryu* pours clarified butter over the oblations on the northern part of the altar. 4.2.2.34. Then these two exchange them: he places the ewe dedicated to the Maruts upon the southern altar, and the ram dedicated to Varuṇa upon the northern altar. He places the ewe dedicated to the Maruts upon the southern altar.

4.2.2.35. The Pratiprasthātṛ pours the clarified butter over the oblation for Varuṇa and that for Ka; the Adhvaryu [pours it] over the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) on the northern [side], not from the *upabhṛt* ladle, for that [ladle] remains empty at the end.
4.2.2.36. He performs the two *ājyabhāga* offerings; the two *ājyabhāgas* are those which slay Vṛtra (*vārtraghnau*).

4.2.2.37. He sits down. [The Adhvaryu says: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, proceed with the oblations on the second altar; recite the invitatory verse for Agni. The Adhvaryu proceeds with the oblations from the Aindrāgna [portion] on the northern altar, saying, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni," while spreading the under-layer of ghee and cutting the portions. 4.2.3 [M117; T1,137] (N1 missing)
4.2.3.1. "Recite for Agni," he says; spreading [the butter], he says—spreading it while cutting off [the portions].
4.2.3.2. The invitatory and offering verses for the five oblations are well-known.
4.2.3.3. "Recite for Indra and Agni," he says; spreading [the butter], he says—spreading it while cutting off [the portions].
4.2.3.4. He recites: “O Indra and Agni, the luminous realms of heaven...

(Ṛgveda 3.1.9). 4.2.3.5. He offers with the verse: “He pierced Vṛtra... (Ṛgveda 6.60.1); when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the oblation. 4.2.3.6. The Adhvaryu sits down; the Hotṛ creeps forward; the Pratiprasthātṛ proceeds with the offering to the Maruts on the southern side.
4.2.3.7. “Recite for the Maruts,” he says; while spreading [the base], he says—while spreading [the base] and cutting [the portions].
4.2.3.8. He cuts once from the ewe, once from the *āmikṣā*, once from the *śamī* leaves, and once from the flour of *karīra* fruits (or the entire *karīra*).
4.2.3.9. He cuts the whole ewe with the subsequent cutting; and of all these, he cuts [the portions].
4.2.3.10. He pours clarified butter over [the oblation] and anoints it back.

4.2.3.118. He recites: "O Maruts, since you from heaven... (*maruto yad dha vo divaḥ*). 4.2.3.129. With the words "The shelter which is yours" (*yā vaḥ śarma*), he performs the *yajati* offering; when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the libation.
4.2.3.13. The Pratiprasthātṛ sits down; the Hotṛ creeps forward. With the offering to Varuṇa and the one to Ka, the Adhvaryu proceeds on the northern side.
4.2.3.14. He says, “Recite the invitatory verse for Varuṇa. [The Adhvaryu], spreading the underlayer of ghee, says this while spreading it and cutting the portion. 4.2.3.15.
In this very manner he cuts portions from these, pours clarified butter over them, and anoints the place from which the portion was cut.
4.2.3.16. He recites the verse, “*ava te heḍa*.
4.2.3.17. With the verse, “*ud uttareṇa... ud uttamam*,” he performs the *yajati* offering; when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the oblation.

4.2.3.18. Saying, “Recite for Kāya,” he says, while spreading the underlayer and pouring the over-layer, as he places the cake on one potsherd (*ekakapāla*) which has been spread with underlayer and poured with overlayer.
4.2.3.19. He recites the verse, “With what [chariot] has Citra appeared for us?

(RV 4.31.1). 4.2.3.20. With the verse, “Who yokes today? he performs the sacrifice; when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering. 4.2.3.21. [The Adhvaryu] says, “Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt! [The Hotṛ], spreading the underlayer [of ghee] while cutting off the portion, says...

4.2.3.22. From the *aindrāgna* [offering], the *adhvaryu* cuts the *sviṣṭakṛt* portion from the oblations on the northern altar. 4.2.3.23. Then he hands it over to the *pratiprasthātṛ*. Having brought that [portion] to the northern altar, the latter cuts the *sviṣṭakṛt* portion from the *māruta* [offering]. 4.2.3.24.

And from the *vāruṇī*, the *kāya*, and the cake on one potsherd (*ekakapāla*), the *adhvaryu* cuts the portions on the northern altar; having poured clarified butter over them twice, he does not anoint them back.
4.2.3.25. The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* meter.

4.2.3.26. He recites [the invitatory verse]: "Do thou gratify... 4.2.3.27. With the words, "O Agni, whatever today of the people's sacrifice, O Hotṛ," he performs the offering; when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the oblation.
4.2.3.28. Having stepped across and set down the two offering-ladles (*srucau*) in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion.
4.2.3.29. Having moved both of them beyond the two altars (*vedī*), he sets them down.
4.2.3.30. Having touched water, the Adhvaryu cuts off the *iḍā* from the oblations on the northern altar for Indra and Agni.
4.2.3.31. Then he takes it up for the Pratiprasthātṛ; having brought it to the northern altar, he cuts off the *iḍā* portion from the oblation for Maruts.
4.2.3.32. And [he cuts off] that for Varuṇa and that for Ka; when the *iḍā* has been invoked on the northern [altar], the Adhvaryu places [the portions] for the Āgnīdhra.
4.2.3.33. They consume [the portions], they perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*), and they carry [the remains] around.
4.2.3.34. When the *prāśitra* has been consumed by the Brahman priest, and [the sacrificer] has consumed his portion of the sacrificial porridge (*caru*), they remove the oblations from the fire.
4.2.3.35. At the *anvāhārya* rice-mess, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite the formula; he sets down the *vājina*.

4.2.3.36. Following the *santati* (continuity), he offers eight *viṣṭambha* (support) and *anvāroha* (ascent) oblations: “To Malimluca svāhā! To Sagara svāhā! To Gaṇaśrī svāhā! To Vibhu svāhā! To Abhibhū svāhā!”—these are the *viṣṭambhas*. “To Nabhas svāhā! To Nabhasya svāhā! To Iṣ svāhā! To Ūrja svāhā!”—these are the *anvārohas*.
4.2.3.37. Having said, "Come, O Sacrificer," while the sacrificer has taken hold [of him], the Hotṛ offers the ninth oblation.
4.2.3.38. Saying, "O Brahman, we shall set forth," the Adhvaryu performs the nine after-offerings (anuyāja) with speckled butter (pṛṣadājya).

4.2.3.39. With what he has left over, the Pratiprasthātṛ comes and, with two *vājavatī* verses, they separate the two offering-spoons (*srucau*). With the *śaṃyu*-formula, they scatter the *prastara* and the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*) together. Having touched water, while pouring [the remnant] into the spoon that was not smeared with clarified butter, he pours in the *vājina*.
4.2.3.40. “Recite for the *vājins*!”—thus says the Adhvaryu as he stands up.
4.2.3.41. He proceeds with the *vājina* in the established manner.

4.2.3.42. He offers to the quarters; he leaves over a portion for consumption. 4.2.3.43. Of that [portion], the Hotṛ first consumes it with the formula: "O Sūryavarcas, partaker of fortune, enter us! O Viśvavin, Lord of the mind, may we be free from distress, may we be wakeful! Then the Adhvaryu [consumes it], then the Brahman and the Pratiprasthātṛ, then the Agnīdh...

Then the Āgnīdhra, then the sacrificer, then the Brahman, then the Āgnīdhra, then the sacrificer. They consume [the portions] with their breaths; for the sacrificer, the consumption is direct. Having gone forth, he performs the joint offerings to the wives.

4.2.3.46. Having offered the *phalīkaraṇa* oblation, having gone toward the east, they offer the *samiṣṭayajus* offerings. "O you two who crush, you two who spread; for Varuṇa, for the scrapings. They collect the scrapings of the other oblations together with the scrapings [of the rice].
4.2.3.47. With the husks and with the scrapings, they go down to the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*).
4.2.3.48. Here, two cords with ten loops are spread out.
4.2.3.49. He recites three times the verses beginning with “uruṃ hi rājā.

4.2.4.110. He recites three times the verse beginning with “uruṃ hi rājā”: “Varuṇa has made wide space for Sūrya... (TS 1.4.45a). 4.2.4.211. With the words “A hundred, O King, are your physicians” (TS 1.4.45b), he causes [the sacrificer] to recite as far as he can see; [he continues] with “A thousand, vast and deep, are your benevolent thoughts; release us from them. (TS 1.4.45b–c).
4.2.4.312. With the words, “The noose of Varuṇa has been stepped upon; [it is] the face of Agni,” he steps onto the edge of the water.

4.2.4.4. Having thrown the *barhis* grass into [the water] with the verse, "The face of Agni has entered into the waters" (1.4.45c,d), he makes an offering over it with: "O Agni, son of the waters, protecting the solar realm in every house, you shall sacrifice the fuel-stick within the waters, svāhā! (or, according to C: "O Agni, son of the waters, protecting the sunless heart in every house, you shall sacrifice the fuel-stick within the waters, svāhā!"). 4.2.4.5. He takes four portions [of clarified butter].

4.2.4.6. He performs four fore-offerings (prayāja) excluding the one with the *barhis* grass-bundle; [he performs] the two butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*). 4.2.4.7. He performs the two butter-portions—the two butter-portions containing the word *apsu*.
4.2.4.8. Saying, "Recite for Agni," he takes four portions of clarified butter while holding the ladle.

4.2.4.9. With the verse, “O Agni, sit in the waters” (*apsv agne*), he recites [the invitatory verse] as before; with the [offering verse], “... the plants ... again,” he performs the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering. He sacrifices with the formula “dhiṣṭavā” accompanied by the word “juṣāṇa. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the oblation. 4.2.4.10.
[The Adhvaryu] says, “Recite for Soma,” while taking four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*).

4.2.4.1113. He recites the verse, “In the waters Soma declared to me,” followed by: “Within [are] all remedies, and Agni who is the source of universal welfare, and the waters which are the universal remedies. (TB 2.5.8.6). 4.2.4.12. He performs the sacrifice with the *juṣāṇa* formula and offers the oblation when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 4.2.4.13. [The Adhvaryu] says, “Recite for Varuṇa”; [the Hotṛ] says while spreading the underlayer of ghee and cutting the portion: [E141]
4.2.4.14. He cuts portions from both the back and the front of the scrapings.

4.2.4.15. He pours clarified butter over them and anoints them [backwards]. 4.2.4.16. He recites, "Hear this my cry, O Varuṇa," and "That I implore of thee"; he offers the oblation at the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*.
4.2.4.17. “Recite for Agni and Varuṇa,” he says; [he offers] the portions that have been spread with a base of ghee and sprinkled with clarified butter.

4.2.4.18. While placing the scrapings (*niṣkāsa*), he recites: “O Agni, you who know, [be our nearest friend] of Varuṇa” (2.5.2.13w, first part). 4.2.4.19. He sacrifices with the verse: “O Agni, be our nearest friend” (2.5.2.13x, part); when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering.
4.2.4.20. He takes four portions of clarified butter. He performs two after-offerings (*anūyāja*), excluding the *barhis* offering.

4.2.4.21. With the formula, “*Avabhṛtha nicaṅkuna*—you are a *nicerur*, a *nicaṅkuṇa*; protect us from what is done by mortals; O divine seer, protect us from the wide space,” he wipes the ladle (*sruk*) downward.
4.2.4.2217. Having offered drops [of water], he consumes the water with his breath, saying: "May the waters and plants be friendly to us; we hate those who are unfriendly toward us. (cf. E143)

4.2.4.23. With the words, "May the plants enter thee gently, as well as the waters," they scatter [the remains] at the *avabhṛtha* (concluding purificatory bath), saying, "O Lord of the Sacrifice, may we serve thee with the sacrifice."

4.2.4.24. With the mantra, “O divine waters, this is your embryo” (1.4.45h), he consecrates the scattered [grains] with the formula: “May he announce you to the gods as well-pleased and well-nourished; may he, being well-pleased and well-nourished, announce us to the gods, O wise one, as such.
4.2.4.25. With the mantra, “The noose of Varuṇa is released; the noose of Varuṇa is cast off” (1.4.45i), he places the two upper woollen-fringed cloths (uttarasicau) upon the waters.
4.2.4.26. With the words, “May I be released from these bonds of Varuṇa,” they should wrap themselves with two garments.

4.2.4.27. With the verse, “O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us” (RV 1.24.15), they loosen the fringe and the girdle, [reciting: “Loosen the lowest; may we be free for Aditi. (The portion *avādhamam ... aditaye syāma* is supplied from RV 1.24.15. “May we be free from the middle one.”

4.2.4.2819. Having stepped down and run along each other's backs, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws up [the cups] with the verse, "ud vayaṃ tamasas pari" (VS 7.1), [reciting]: "seeing the highest light, seeing the supreme."

4.2.4.29. With the formula, “Fuel art thou; may we thrive through thee” (ŚB 1.4.45k), they prepare the *audumbarī* fuel-sticks. Having prepared the fuel-sticks, they return without looking back, saying, “Fuel art thou; splendor art thou; bestow splendor upon me” (ŚB 1.4.45k). 4.2.4.30.
The sacrificer places [the fuel-stick] on the *āhavanīya* fire; in the same manner, the wife [places one] on the *gārhapatya* fire.
4.2.4.31. With the words, “I have followed the waters” (TS 1.4.45), he causes these two [fires] to stand near him with the formula, “We have united with sap, with splendor.
4.2.4.32. Having returned, he merges the former fire into the latter Āhavanīya fire; following the conclusion of the oblation, he turns back.
4.2.4.33. The ritual materials are well-known.

4.2.4.3420. "He who turned the Gharma around along the ends of the earth—with the sharp flame of Agni, with the brilliance of Vaiśvānara, I turn you around; with truth I turn you around; with auspiciousness I turn you toward me. May that be *ṛta*, may that be truth, may that be my vow; may I be able through it, may I be capable through it, may I succeed through it"—with these words, [he says]: "Agni with his sharp flame, with the brilliance of Vaiśvānara, [turns] you."

"I turn back by means of truth; I turn around by means of auspiciousness; I bring you near by means of well-being. May that be the *ṛta*, may that be the *satya*, may that be the vow; may I be able to accomplish it through that, may I prosper thereby. With these words, he first shaves the hair on the front part. Then on the right side, then on the back, then on the left side, and then in the middle.
Following the conclusion of the oblation, he performs the sacrifice with the established full-moon oblation (*paurṇamāsa-havis*).
4.2.4.37. He performs the *devavrata* vows. [E147] {C: || 8 || ; thus ends the second *anuvāka*; T1:
|| } 4.3.1(C)/4.2.5(T1) [M122;T1,142] (N1,40a begins at 4.3.1.20) {T1 has at the beginning "devavratāni carati". If this reading were adopted, then the section would be 4.2.5 rather than 4.3.1.}

4.3.1.121. "Tomorrow there will be the full moon with the Kṛttikās. Having set out the sacrificial implements and brought forward the waters, he offers a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Anīkavant while the sun is rising. 4.3.1.2. Once the offering has been made, he recites the Prāṇagraha formulas and the Pṛśni verses. 4.3.1.3. When [the oblation] has been placed near, he recites the Apānagraha formulas, the Pṛśni verses, and the Daśahotṛ formula.
4.3.1.4. For this [offering], the two *ājyabhāga* portions belong to the slayers of Vṛtra.

4.3.1.5. "Recite for Agni Anīkavant! he says; while spreading the base-layer of butter and cutting the portion, he says: 4.3.1.6. "O Agni, auspicious is your appearance, O you of beautiful countenance," he recites. (4.3.1.3c)

4.3.1.723. With the verse, “Auspicious is your face, O Agni, O powerful one,” he performs the sacrifice; when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation. 4.3.1.8. The two *saṃyājyā* verses are [the dual forms] *śardhasvatyau*.

4.3.1.924. He recites the invitatory verse: “The beloved house-friend, the guest of the dwelling...”—he recites thus—“O Agni, come to this our sacrifice, you who know; [overcome] all rival peoples. (Note: The phrase *anvāhemān no ... bhajanānīti* is supplied from the *TB*.)

4.3.1.1025. With the words, “O Agni, be strong for great good fortune,” he performs the sacrifice; with the words, “Thy splendors are most excellent, thy greatnesses,” he offers the oblation when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.
4.3.1.11. He offers the oblation following the continuity of the Hotṛ’s offering. 4.3.1.12. The rite is successfully accomplished; this sacrifice comes to a conclusion.

4.3.1.13. Having set out the sacrificial implements and having carried forward the ritual waters, he offers a *caru* oblation to the Maruts Sāntapana at the midday pressing. 4.3.1.14. Once the oblation has been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.
4.3.1.15. When it has been placed on the fire, he recites the *apānagraha* formulas, the *pṛśni* verses, and the *daśahotṛ* formula for the Maruts.
4.3.1.16. For this [offering], the two portions of clarified butter (*ājyabhāgau*) proceed with the *pradhāna* (principal offerings).

4.3.1.17. Saying, “Recite for the Maruts who are the Sāntapanas,” he says [this] while spreading [the underlayer of ghee]; saying [this] while spreading [it], he cuts off [the portion]. 4.3.1.18. He recites the invitatory verse: “O Sāntapanas, this is the oblation” (4.3.13k).

4.3.1.19. He sacrifices with the verse, “The Maruts, who are of the year, are well-praising, well-praising” (4.3.13m). At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation. 4.3.1.20. The two *saṃyājyā* verses contain the word *svasti*.
4.3.1.21. He recites the verse, “May there be well-being for us from heaven and from earth, O Agni” (4.3.13f).
4.3.1.22. He sacrifices with [the formula]: “O Hotṛ, those deities of Manu, thus. 4.3.1.23.
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation.
4.3.1.24. At the time of the throwing [of the ladle], he turns the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*) around; he turns the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) down.
4.3.1.23. He offers the oblation following the continuity of the Hotṛ’s recitation.

4.3.1.24. The rite is successfully accomplished; this iṣṭi comes to a conclusion. 4.3.1.25. With the pot from which the water has been poured out and with the rice grains that have been washed away, he awaits the cows as they come toward him.
4.3.1.26. In the evening, he milks all the cows and cooks the *gṛhamedhīya* sacrificial pap (*caru*) on the *gārhapatya* fire.

4.3.1.27. Once it has been cooked, he draws out three portions of the boiled rice (*odana*), each underlain by a layer of clarified butter (*upastīrṇa*) and sprinkled over with clarified butter (*abhighārita*). 4.3.1.28. He pours a large amount of clarified butter over the first portion.
4.3.1.29. Then he pours [the remnant] over the other two [paridhis].
4.3.1.30. Having offered [the oblation], the Adhvaryu, having run forward, joins together the enclosing sticks (paridhis).
4.3.1.31. They bring the cooked rice dishes; he places the first one that was removed from the center in the vessel of the *dhruvā* ladle.
4.3.1.32. Therefore, he offers the two *ājyabhāga* (clarified butter portions). Therefore, there is the under-sprinkling and the over-sprinkling on the south and on the north.
4.3.1.33. He offers the other two *ājyabhāgas*, which are the two *ājyabhāgas* possessed of wealth (*rayimantau*).
4.3.1.34. While taking four portions of clarified butter, he says: "Recite for Agni," while taking four portions of clarified butter.
4.3.1.35. He recites: "By Agni may he obtain wealth" (*agninā rayim aśnavat*).
4.3.1.36. He performs the sacrifice with the *juṣāṇa* formula. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation.
4.3.1.37. Saying, "Recite for Śoma," while taking four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*), he...
4.3.1.38. He recites: "O Gayasphāna, bring these hither. 4.3.1.39. He performs the sacrifice with the *juṣāṇa* formula; when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering. 4.3.1.40.
While spreading the under-layer of butter and cutting the portions, he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for the Maruts, the Gṛhamedhins! and then: "Recite the invitatory verse for the Gṛhamedhins!"
4.3.1.41. He cuts portions from the middle of the rice-oblation, both from behind and from the front; in the same manner he cuts from the southern half, and likewise from the northern half.
4.3.1.42. He pours clarified butter over them and anoints them back.
4.3.1.43. He recites: "O householders, come hither."
4.3.1.44. He recites the verse, “Your great powers rise up from the depths,” and offers the oblation when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered.
4.3.1.45. Saying, “Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt,” he spreads a layer of clarified butter and takes the portions while cutting them off.
4.3.1.46. He cuts once from the northern half of the middle portion of the boiled rice; likewise from the southern half, and likewise from the northern half.
4.3.1.47. He pours clarified butter over it twice; he does not anoint it back. 4.3.1.48. He recites as the two *saṃyājyā* verses: "O Agni, kindled, shine forth... 4.3.1.49.
He performs the *yajati* offering with the verse: "O Agni, these most pleasing oblations... At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the libation.

4.3.1.50. Having gathered these enclosing-sticks (paridhi), he throws them into the fire. He makes an offering over them with the residue of the oblation. 4.3.1.51. Having stepped across to his proper place and set down the two offering-spoons (srucau) in their respective places, he cuts portions for the *iḍā* from the middle rice-mass and from the other two.
4.3.1.52. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he hands over the northern rice-mass to the *agnīdh*.
4.3.1.53. They consume the *dakṣiṇā* for the Brahman priest. They perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*). 4.3.1.E. From this point on, he offers the *agnihotra*.
4.3.2.1. From this point on, he performs the *agnihotra* sacrifice itself.
4.3.2.2. Whatever remains in the cooking pot, of that the *adhvaryu* and the sacrificer (*yajamāna*) partake.
4.3.2.3. Others cook it as a neighborly gift for the wife.
4.3.2.4. He eats that [food]. 4.3.2.5. They anoint themselves; they rub themselves with ointment. 4.3.2.6. They let the calves stay with their mothers.
4.3.2.7. Having brought the residue from the vessel with clarified butter, he places it near the Gārhapatya fire.
4.3.2.8. The sacrificer himself should attend to that [residue], thinking, "This is its morning portion. This indeed is its morning portion. 4.3.2.9.
After the Adhvaryu has offered the Agnihotra, he offers a full-spoon oblation upon the Gārhapatya fire, having spread a base of butter and poured butter over it, following the bellowing of the bull.

4.3.2.10. Standing behind the fire, he recites the *puro’nuvākyā* [invitatory verse] beginning with: “*pūrṇā darvir ā pṛṇīhi* (1.8.4b). 4.3.2.11. He performs the *yajyā* [offering verse] with: “*supūrṇā śatakrato* (1.8.4b) ... *dehi me* (1.8.4c); *dadāmi te niharāmi te svāhā* (1.8.4c with variation). Thus: “*supūrṇā śatakrato*, ‘O Śatakratu, give [to me]!’, ‘I give to you, I deliver to you, svāhā! (1.8.4c with variation).
4.3.2.12. At this time, the sacrificer should bellow like a bull.
4.3.2.13. Regarding this, they say: "That which is done with a bull is difficult to accomplish and difficult to agree upon.
4.3.2.14. He offers the oblation, saying: "Svāhā!"

4.3.2.15. Having arranged the sacrificial implements and having led forward the waters, he offers a cake on seven potsherds to the Maruts, the Playful Ones (krīḍin), simultaneously with the rising of the sun. 4.3.2.16. Once the offering has been set out, he recites the Prāṇagrahas and the Pṛśnis.
4.3.2.17. When [the oblation] has been placed near [the fire], he recites the Apānagrahas, the Pṛśnis, and the Daśahotṛ formula.
4.3.2.18. For this [offering], the two *ājyabhāga* portions are dedicated to Vṛtrahan.
4.3.2.19. While spreading the base layer of clarified butter and cutting the portion, he says: “Recite for the Maruts, the sportive ones! 4.3.2.20. He recites:
“The sportive host of the Maruts... (VS 27.34).
4.3.2.21. He offers with the verse, “Like swift horses are the Maruts... (RV 5.54.10), and he makes the oblation when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered.
4.3.2.22. The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
4.3.2.23. He makes the oblation following the continuous flow (*santati*) of the Hotṛ’s offering.

4.3.2.24. The ritual action is accomplished; this sacrifice is concluded. 4.3.2.25. Therefore, it is indeed the Mahāhavis [sacrifice]. 4.3.2.26. To the east of the Āhavanīya fire, the altar (vedi) is prepared, having space sufficient for a chariot.
4.3.2.27. He carries away the *staṃbayajus* (the sacrificial grass from the stump).
4.3.2.28. He draws out the altar (*vedi*) and mutters the *karaṇa* formula.
4.3.2.29. He issues the call: "The wooden sword (*sphya*), the water-vessel—bring the *śamyā* wood! Come, O sacrificer! O Āgnīdhra, sit down by the high altar (*uttaravedi*)."
4.3.2.30. Following the procedure for the *uttaravedi*, he pours out the earth for the *uttaravedi*.
4.3.2.31. They kindle the fuel; they prepare the supporting ladles; following the procedure for the fire, he throws the fire [into the pit]. 4.3.2.32.
Following the procedure for the fire, he throws the fire [into the pit].
4.3.2.33. The ritual succeeds through the *atimukti* offerings.
4.3.2.34. Having offered the *atimukti* oblations, having arranged the sacrificial implements, and having brought forward the waters, he pours out the *mahāhavis*: a cake on eight potsherds for Agni.
4.3.3 [The Mahāhavis].

4.3.3.1. [An offering] on eight potsherds for Agni; a pap for Sūrya; a cake on twelve potsherds for Savitṛ; a pap for Sarasvatī; a pap for Pūṣan; a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra-Agni; a pap for Sūrya; a cake on twelve potsherds for Savitṛ; a pap for Sarasvatī; a pap for Pūṣan; a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra-Agni; a pap for Indra; and a cake on one potsherd for Viśvakarman. 4.3.3.2. Once the grains have been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagrahas* and the *pṛśnis*.

4.3.3.3. Having released his speech at the call to the *haviṣkṛt*, he offers the *pañcahotṛ* formula with four ladlings of ghee into the *āhavanīya* fire. 4.3.3.4. The sacrificial oblations (*havīṃṣi*) are cooked.
4.3.3.5. When the oblations are cooked, he takes up the wooden sword (*sphya*), saying: "O Brahman, I shall perform the second tracing (*uttaraṃ parigrāham*)."

4.3.3.6. Once the impulse has been given, he performs the second tracing around. 4.3.3.7. Having leveled the ground and propped it up, he issues the command: "Place the sprinkling waters; set down the fuel and the sacrificial grass; wipe the dipping-spoon and the offering-ladles; gird the wife; come forth with the clarified butter!"—[that is,] "Place the sprinkling waters; set down the fuel and the sacrificial grass; wipe the dipping-spoon and the offering-ladles; gird the wife; come forth with the clarified butter; bring the curds for the speckled butter; come, O sacrificer!"
4.3.3.8. They perform this: they sprinkle the fuel and the sacrificial grass with the speckled butter.
4.3.3.9. Having wiped the offering-ladles, he takes up the clarified butters, including the speckled butter.
4.3.3.10. He sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass; he sprinkles the altar; he sprinkles what has been placed near.
4.3.3.11. Having poured out the water, he takes the *prastara* bundle; he spreads the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). 4.3.3.12.
Having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) and places two fuel-sticks (*samidh*) upon them.
4.3.3.13. Having caused the sacrificer to recite over the enclosing sticks, he yokes the fire.
4.3.3.14. Having come, he places [the *āmikṣā*] crosswise; the *prastara* on the two crosswise [straw-mats], the *juhū* on the *prastara*, and the other two spoons (*barhis*) on the [other] two.
4.3.3.15. They adorn [the offerings].
They set down the sacrificial oblations (*havis*) one after another, having first spread a base of ghee and then poured ghee over them.

4.3.3.16. Having sprinkled the sacrificial oblations (*havīṃṣi*) with clarified butter, they bring them forward. 4.3.3.17. When [the cups] have been set down, he recites the *pānagraha*, the *praśni*, and the *apānagraha* formulas. 4.3.3.18. Having touched [the vessels] together with the formula, "The steadfast ones have sat down; that which is mine, O Agni... (cf. MS 1.1.12:8.3; KS 1.11:6; VS 2.6), he recites the *pañcahotṛ* formula.
4.3.3.19. He proceeds with the fire produced by friction. 4.3.3.20. He recites the invitatory formula for the fire being kindled. 4.3.3.21. He recites seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses.

4.3.3.22. When the *sāmidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* spoon, he says: "O Āgnīdh, cleanse the fire thrice with each [ladle]"—[meaning] "cleanse the northern fire thrice with each of the two ladles. 4.3.3.23. Having crossed over with the two ladles without letting them touch, and having anointed the *dhruvā* and set it down, he chooses the *pravara*. The Hotṛ sits down. 4.3.3.24. The Hotṛ sits down. He chooses the *pravara*, saying: "The *dhruvā* has sat down; that which is mine, O Agni... [and so on]. He then chooses the *pravara*. The Hotṛ sits down.
4.3.3.25. Being impelled, he takes up the two offering-spoons. He performs the *prayāja* offerings.
4.3.3.26. He says, “O Śrauṣaṭ! Make it heard!”—“Sacrifice the fuel-sticks (*śam̐idh*)”—and “Sacrifice! Sacrifice! 4.3.3.27.
Having poured half into the fourth [offering], he pours the whole into the eighth.
4.3.3.28. He offers all the *prayāja* oblations from the *upabhṛt* ladle.
4.3.3.29. Having performed the *prayājas* and stepped across, he pours clarified butter over the *dhruvā* ladle.
4.3.3.30. He pours the *pṛṣadājya* (clotted butter) over the sacrificial offerings in successive order, but at the end, not over the *upabhṛt*; for that [ladle] remains empty.

4.3.3.31. He offers the two portions of clarified butter (*ājyabhāgau*). The two *ājyabhāga* offerings belong to Vṛtrahan. 4.3.3.32. "Recite for Agni," he says, while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portion]. {N1 has an "EM"; C: || 11 ||}
He says, "Recite for Agni," while spreading [the clarified butter] and cutting [the portions]. 4.3.4.2.
The invitatory verses (*puronuvākyā*) and offering verses (*yājyā*) for the six oblations are well-known.
4.3.4.3. He says, "Recite for Indra," while spreading the underlayer and cutting the portion.
4.3.4.4. He recites after [the invitatory verse]: "O Indra, [bring] winning wealth" (Ṛgveda 1.8.1).
4.3.4.5. He offers the oblation with the words, "Thou hast overcome" (*pra sasāhiṣe*), and pours it when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.

4.3.4.6. “Recite for Viśvakarman,” he says; [the Adhvaryu], spreading the underlayer, says; having spread the underlayer and poured the clarified butter over it, while placing the cake on one potsherd, [he acts].

4.3.4.7. “O Viśvakarman, increasing by the oblation” (or “O Viśvakarman, increasing with the oblation”), he recites; “O Viśvakarman, by the increasing oblation,” he offers. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 4.3.4.8. “Recite for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt,” he says; [the Adhvaryu], spreading the underlayer and cutting off portions [of the cake], [acts].
4.3.4.9. He cuts a portion once from the northern half of each of all the sacrificial oblations.
4.3.4.10. Having cut a portion of the cake baked on one potsherd (*ekakapāla*) from its receptacle, he pours clarified butter over it twice; he does not anoint it back. 4.3.4.11.
The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* meter.

4.3.4.12. He recites, “Do thou gratify,” and sacrifices with the verse, “O Agni, whatever today of the people’s sacrifice, O Hotṛ. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 4.3.4.13. Having stepped across and placed the two ladles in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion. 4.3.4.14. Having touched water, he cuts off the *iḍā* portion.
4.3.4.15. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places [the portion] for the *agnīdh*.

4.3.4.16. They consume it; they sprinkle themselves; they carry it around. 4.3.4.17. When the *brahmán* has consumed his share, having thrown the sacrificer’s portion into the *prāśitra* rice-porridge, they remove it from the fire.
4.3.4.18. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite over the oblations at the *anvāhārya* (funeral feast).

4.3.4.19. Following the continuity, he offers eight *viṣṭambha-anvāroha* oblations: "To the *śaṃsarpa*, svāhā! To the eye, svāhā! To Sūrya, svāhā! To Candramas, svāhā!"—these are the *viṣṭambhas*. "To the *śahasa*, svāhā! To the *sahasya*, svāhā! To the *tapas*, svāhā! To the *tapasya*, svāhā!"—these are the *anvārohas*.
4.3.4.20. Having said, "Come, O sacrificer," while the sacrificer has taken hold of him, he offers the ninth oblation for the Hotṛ.
4.3.4.21. Saying, "O Brahman, we shall set forth," he performs the nine after-offerings with the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya).
4.3.4.22. Having returned, he separates the two offering-spoons with the two Vājavatī verses.
4.3.4.23. With the *śaṃyu*-formula, he scatters the *prastara* and the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) together. 4.3.4.24. Having gone outside, they perform the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings.
4.3.4.25. Having offered the *phalīkaraṇa* oblation and having stepped forward toward the east, he offers three *samiṣṭayajus* oblations.

4.3.4.26. Having offered with the *sruva* ladle, saying, “O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice, O hero, *svāhā*” (1.4.44g), and having replenished the *dhruvā* vessel, he offers with the *sruc* ladle, saying, “O gods who know the way” (1.4.44i–k), [and] “Having found the way, place [it] in the wind” (*gātuṃ vittvā vāte dhā*). [cf. E62] 4.3.4.27. The rite is successfully accomplished. 4.3.4.28. The Great Oblation (*mahāhavis*) is concluded.
Thus ends the third section (anuvāka).
4.4.1 [The Mahāpitṛyajña]:
From this point on, it is indeed the Pitṛyajña.

4.4.1.2. Its materials are: rice and barley, *cāmbarīṣa* (and) *cāmbarīṣa*, the milk of a cow that has recently calved, a stalk of sugarcane, a root-cutter, a sacrificial altar (*vedi*) dug out to provide space for a couch (*talpa*), measuring a man’s height, four-cornered, and level on all sides.

A water-jar with ten openings, a long sacrificial fuel-stick, sacrificial grass together with its roots, collyrium, ointment, a mattress, a pillow, and a screen. Having arranged the sacrificial implements to the south of the *gārhapatya* fire and having carried forward the water, he offers a six-potsherd cake to Soma accompanied by the Fathers (*pitṛmat*), and parched grains (*dhānāḥ*) to the Fathers seated on the sacrificial grass (*barhiṣad*).

4.4.1.4. For the *pitṛ*s who have been consumed by fire (*agniṣvātta*), they pound [the grain] for a stirred offering (*mantha*) made from the milk of a cow that has calved recently (*abhivānyā*). They pound it to the south of the *gārhapatya* fire.
4.4.1.5. On the southern half of the *gārhapatya* altar, he places six potsherds.

4.4.1.6. On the northern half [of the fire], he bakes single-pot-sherd cakes for Tryambaka—one for each person—with one cake left over. He roasts parched grains (*dhānā*) on the *ānvāhāryapacana* fire using a frying pan (*ambarīṣa*). Having enclosed them, he divides them into two parts.
4.4.1.7. From those [parched grains], they prepare half as groats (*saktu*).
4.4.1.8. Having wiped the *sruva* and *sruk* ladles at the *anvāhāryapacana* fire, he takes portions of clarified butter. 4.4.1.9.
They bring all six [portions] taken in six ladlings. 4.4.1.10.
For him, they bring half of the *puroḍāśa* cake from the *anvāhāryapacana* fire, with the base-layered butter spread beneath and the top-layered butter poured over it.
4.4.1.11. Its adornment is that they mix parched grains with clarified butter and bring them forward.
4.4.1.12. That is their adornment: having milked the cow that has been approached for milking, he stirs a mash into half a vessel with a stalk of sugarcane.

4.4.1.13. Turning to the right without taking hold [of the fire], he places the *anvāhāryapacana* fire upon it as its ornament; having taken the fire from the *anvāhāryapacana*, he places it upon the altar (*vedi*) and kindles it. 4.4.1.14.
He mentally performs the *staṃbayajus* rite for that [altar].
4.4.1.15. He encloses the altar. He mutters the *karaṇa* formula.
4.4.1.16. Having brought a water-pot, he places it on the right shoulder.
4.4.1.17. Having brought sacrificial grass together with its roots, he places it to the north in the very same manner.
4.4.1.18. Having brought a longer fuel-stick, he places it to the north in the very same manner.
4.4.1.19. Taking up a water-pot, the sprinkler goes around three times, sprinkling [water] counter-clockwise, and having placed it down, he goes around.
4.4.1.20. Having set down the pot, he runs back again three times along the path.
4.4.1.21. Taking up sacrificial grass together with its roots, he goes around three times, spreading it counter-clockwise.

4.4.1.22. Having laid down the *prastara* grass-bundle, he runs back three times along the same path. 4.4.1.23. Taking up the *prastara*, having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
4.4.1.24. He places the fuel-sticks (*samidh*) upon the fire.
4.4.1.25. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), he yokes the fire.
4.4.1.26. To the west of the fire, he places the *prastara* grass-bundle.
4.4.1.27. They themselves bring the *barhis* grass across [the altar].

4.4.1.28. From this [set], they bring forth one by one in succession: one *dhruvā* ladle, one *sruva* ladle, one *juhū* ladle, one *upabhṛt* ladle, one *dhruvā* ladle, one vessel for clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*), one vessel for the *prāśitra* portion, one *mekṣaṇa* stirring-spoon, one *puroḍāśa* cake, one portion of parched grain (*dhānā*), one *mantha* mixture, one stalk of sugarcane, one collyrium, one ointment, one mattress (*kaśipu*), one pillow (*upabarhaṇa*), and one curtain (*pariśrayaṇa*).
They bring these out one by one in sequence.

4.4.1.29. Having approached and touched [the fire] while reciting, “The steadfast ones have sat down; that which is mine, O Agni... (cf. MS 1.1.12:8.3; KS 1.11:6; VS 2.6), he recites the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula. 4.4.1.30. “[Recite for Agni, for the gods, for the ancestors, who is being kindled! 4.4.1.31.
He recites three times these verses beginning with, “Desiring you, we invoke you” (2.6.12a): “Desiring, may we kindle you... [2.6.12a] ...you who eat.”
4.4.1.32. He desires to encompass those [sacrificial grasses] with fuel-sticks and leaves one [stick] over as a kindling-stick (samidh).

4.4.1.33. When the *sāmidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* spoon, he says: "Wipe the fire once, wipe it once! (*saṃmṛḍḍhi*). 4.4.1.34. Having stood up, he chooses the *pravara*.

4.4.1.35. He says, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard" (*o śrāvaya*), which is [equivalent to] "cause to hear" (*āśrāvaya*). "Sit down" (*sīda*)—this alone is the *pravara* (ancestral invocation) here; he does not choose a lineage (*ārṣeya*) nor a *hotṛ* priest.
4.4.1.36. The *hotṛ* sits down. 4.4.1.37. Being impelled (*prasūta*), he takes up the two offering-spoons (*sruc*).
4.4.1.38. He performs four fore-offerings (prayāja) excluding the one for the *barhis* grass.
4.4.1.39. He performs the two butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*); [the two] butter-portions contain the word "living" (*jīvat*).
4.4.1.40. Saying, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni," he takes four portions of clarified butter.

4.4.1.41. He recites the verse: “O Agni, come to us with fair splendor. 4.4.1.42. With the verse, “Wealth for all life, wealth for living,” he performs the sacrifice with the *juṣāṇa* formula; when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation.
4.4.1.43. Saying, “Recite the invitatory prayer for Soma,” he takes four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*) itself.

4.4.1.44. He recites: “O Soma, you [are] great fortune... (tvaṃ soma mahe bhagam), and [the verse]: “You... for the sake of life” (tvaṃ dhūna ṛtā=jīvasa). 4.4.1.45. He performs the sacrifice with the [verse] beginning with *juṣāṇa* (being pleased); he offers the oblation when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 4.4.1.46.

Having stepped across and placed the two offering-spoons (*srucau*) in their respective places, they put on the sacred threads over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītāni*) and take them up. (Note: N₁ contains an "EM"; C: || 13 ||)
While they are arranging the *prācīnāvīta* [mode of wearing the sacred thread], 4.4.2.1. he takes up the southern enclosing-stick (*dakṣiṇārdhya paridhi*).
4.4.2.3. He lays it down along that middle enclosing-stick.
4.4.2.4. They enclose [the altar].
4.4.2.5. They join the connection of the enclosure opposite the northern corner of the altar.
4.4.2.6. They turn around.
4.4.2.7. To the north, the Brahman and the sacrificer sit down; to the south, the Hotṛ and the Āgnīdhra. Having taken a portion from the south, he goes northward. 4.4.2.7. He paces back and forth.
4.4.2.8. He causes the announcement with “*āsvadhā*”; he responds with “*astu svadhā*. 4.4.2.9.
He utters the *vaṣaṭ* call with “*svadhā namaḥ*. 4.4.2.10.
While spreading the underlayer and cutting the portions, he says, “Perform the *svadhā* for Soma accompanied by the ancestors (*pitṛmat*).”
4.4.2.11. He cuts off a single portion from the *puroḍāśa*, a single portion from the roasted grains (*dhānā*), and a single portion from the stirred drink (*mantha*).
4.4.2.12. He sprinkles clarified butter over them and anoints them back.
4.4.2.13. He recites two *puronuvākyās* for each [offering]: "{O Soma, you are wise through your insight... may you become our liberal patron}" (TS 2.6.12.1b,c).
4.4.2.14. He causes the announcement to be made with “*Āsvadhā!*”; he responds with “*Astu svadhā!*” (Let there be *svadhā*). 4.4.2.15. He says, “Make *svadhā* for Soma accompanied by the ancestors.
4.4.2.16. He takes the vow with the words, “Those who [partake of] *svadhā*.”
4.4.2.17. He sacrifices with the verse, “O Soma, being in agreement with the fathers... (RV 2.6.12d), [and] with the words, “...according to heaven... of riches” (RV 2.6.12d). 4.4.2.18.
He utters the *vaṣaṭ* call with the words, “*śvadhā namaḥ*” (Svadhā! Adoration!). When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering. 4.4.2.19.
While spreading the under-layer of butter and while cutting the portion, he says, “*pitṛbhyo barhiṣadbhyo ’nusvadhākurv*. (To the fathers seated on the sacrificial grass, saying *anusvadhā*.)
4.4.2.20. He cuts off the parched grains (*dhānā*) once; he cuts off the stirred drink (*mantha*) once; he cuts off the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) once.

4.4.2.21. He pours clarified butter over them. He anoints them back [with ghee]. 4.4.2.22. He recites the invitatory verse: “O Fathers, seated on the sacrificial grass, come hither with your aid” (RV 2.6.12f,g), ending with: “these offerings for you... come most readily. (As in N1 and C: *anvāhemā vo havyā gamiṣṭhā*.)
4.4.2.23. He causes the announcement to be made with, “Let there be *svadhā*! and he responds with the counter-announcement, “Let there be *svadhā*!
4.4.2.24. He says, “O Fathers seated on the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), pronounce *svadhā*!
4.4.2.25. They respond with the formula, “Those who [are here], let there be *svadhā*!”

4.4.2.26–27. He performs the *yajati* offering with the verse: "{N1: Upahūtā . . . s somyāsa} ‘The Soma-loving fathers have been invited’ (2.6.12h). {Thus N1; C: “barhiṣye=te alan tvasmān”}. 4.4.2.27. With the words “svadhā namaḥ,” he utters the *vaṣaṭ* call. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the oblation. 4.4.2.28. While spreading the under-layer and cutting the portions, he says: “To the fathers, those consumed by Agni, let there be the *svadhā*! (2.6.12.3h). [E239f.]
4.4.2.29. He cuts off a single portion from the stirred offering (mantha), a single portion from the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa), and a single portion from the parched grains (dhānā). 4.4.2.30.
He pours clarified butter over them and anoints them back.

4.4.2.3128. He recites: “May our Soma-loving ancestors hear us” (RV X.15.1); “The Agniṣvātta [Agniṣvātta] fathers, in harmony with the seasons, enjoying their portion, may they accept the offered oblations; then may they bestow prosperity upon us. Enjoying the porridge (*karambha*) milked from the barren cow, rising up—both those who are near and those who are far—the Agniṣvātta fathers, in harmony with the seasons, having sat down upon this sacrificial grass (*barhis*), may they rejoice. (RV X.15.9–10).
4.4.2.32. He causes the announcement with “*āsvadhā*”; he responds with “*astu svadhā*. 4.4.2.33.
He says, “Make *svadhā* for the *Agniṣvātta* Pitṛs! They respond with the *āguḥ* formula: “*Ye svadhā*. 4.4.2.34.

He performs the sacrifice with, “Having come, O Pitṛs, may they rejoice! [He continues: “The *Agniṣvātta*s, being in harmony with the seasons, rising up—those who have gone to this world, those who have departed, the non-malicious ones who know the *ṛta*.”
4.4.2.35. He utters the *vaṣaṭ* with the formula, “*Śvadhā namaḥ*. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers the oblation.

4.4.2.36. While spreading a base of clarified butter and cutting portions, he says, “To Agni Kavyavāhana, *anusvadhā*! 4.4.2.37. He cuts a single portion from the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), a single portion from the parched grains (*dhānā*), and a single portion from the stirred drink (*mantha*) using a stalk of sugarcane.

4.4.2.38. Having placed that [ladle] down, he hands the two ladles to the *agnīdh* one after another. 4.4.2.39. He pours the clarified butter over them twice; he does not anoint them back. 4.4.2.40. He recites:

“O Agni, carrier of the offerings to the ancestors (*kavyavāhana*)... (RV 2.6.12), followed by: “He shall worship the fathers who increase the cosmic order... for the fathers... those who are in the three worlds... (TB 2.6.16.2).

"O you who increase the cosmic order, come from the presence of the Fathers who sit at the *gharma*—those who, speeding toward the gods, have increased the *hotrā*, being fashioned by hymns with their songs. O Agni, come hither with those well-disposed ones, with the true *kavyas*, the Fathers who sit at the *gharma*.
(4.4.2.41) He causes the announcement to be made with "Svadhā! He causes the response to be made with "Let there be Svadhā!"

4.4.2.42. He says, "Make Agni Kavyavāhana [the bearer of offerings to the ancestors] *svadhā*. He consecrates himself with the words, "Those for whom there is *svadhā*. 4.4.2.43. With the words, "The bearer of oblations (*havyavāha*)," he sacrifices, [reciting]: "May he, the imperishable, much-beloved Agni, being honored with clarified butter as the sacrificial offering, the one who approaches the ancestors as the bearer of *kavya*, fulfill our progeny with heroic sons. 4.4.2.44. He utters the *vaṣaṭ* call with the words, "*Svadhā namaḥ*. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the oblation.
4.4.2.45. The Āgnīdhra throws the stalks of sugarcane [into the fire]; he offers them with the residue of the oblation.
4.4.2.46. Having stepped across and placed the two offering-spoons in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion.
4.4.2.47. He moves it to the north and places it there.
4.4.2.48. Having touched water, he cuts off the *iḍā* portion.
4.4.2.49. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places it for the *agnīdh*.
4.4.2.50. He smells the fires; he does not eat them; he performs the ritual purification (*mārjana*).
