4.4.2.51. The Brahman smells [the portions], but does not eat; he wipes [his mouth]. The Hotṛ smells [the portions], but does not eat; he wipes [his mouth]. 4.4.2.52.
They scatter those [portions] right here into the *iḍā*-vessel.
4.4.2.E. Then he pours out three water-vessels.

Then he pours out three water-pots. 4.4.3.2. With the words, “May the fathers cleanse themselves,” he pours on the southern buttock; with the words, “May the grandfathers cleanse themselves,” on the right shoulder; and with the words, “May the great-grandfathers cleanse themselves,” on the left shoulder.
4.4.3.3. He says, “Wipe it clean,” and spreads [the butter] in the joined palms of the sacrificer.
4.4.3.4. He cuts off a single portion from the sacrificial cake, a single portion from the parched grains, and a single portion from the stirred drink.
4.4.3.5. He sprinkles [the portions] with clarified butter.

4.4.3.6. With the words, “This for you, father,” he gives [the portion] on the southern hip, saying: “Those whom you follow, and those who follow you, and those who are around you, and those who dwell with you along with the *svadhā*.

4.4.3.7. Having approached the front of the fire with the words, “This is ours,” he touches the northern hip of the altar with the words: “May we, being living and alive, move along this [earth] and be united.
4.4.3.8. He indeed spreads [an offering] into his joined palms.

4.4.3.9. He cuts off a single portion of the parched grains, a single portion of the stirred drink, and a single portion of the sacrificial cake. 4.4.3.10. He pours clarified butter over them. 4.4.3.11.

With the words, “This for you, grandfather,” he places it on the northern shoulder [or, according to C, the southern shoulder], saying: “And those whom you follow, and those who follow you—those who are around you and those who dwell with you in the *svadhā*—[this is] the *svadhā*-dwelling. [N1,44a6]

4.4.3.12. Having approached the fire from the front with the words, "This is ours," he touches the northern corner of the altar with the formula: "May we, being living and moving along this [earth], become long-lived.
4.4.3.13. He indeed places [the food] into his cupped hands.
4.4.3.14. He takes a single portion of the stirred drink (*mantha*), a single portion of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), and a single portion of the parched grains (*dhānā*).
4.4.3.15. He pours clarified butter over [the portion].

4.4.3.16. With the words, “This for you, great-grandfather,” he places it on the northern shoulder, saying: “Those whom you follow, and those who follow you, and those who are around you—those whom you accompany, those who surround you, and those with whom you share the *svadhā*, O dweller in the *svadhā*.”

4.4.3.17. Having approached the fire from the east with the words, "This is ours," he touches the northern corner of the altar with the mantra: "May we, being alive, move along this [earth] while living.
4.4.3.18. The sacrificer performs the purification (*mārjana*). 4.4.3.19. Having said, "O fathers, rejoice here according to your respective portions," they go out toward the north.

4.4.3.20. They remain standing until he has finished. 4.4.3.21. With the verse, “O you of beautiful appearance, we [approach] you” (1.8.5c), he breathes over the Āhavanīya fire with the words, “O Maghavan, may we gladden you.

4.4.3.22. With the verse, “Now indeed, O chariot with full seat,” he approaches it from that very spot with the words, “Praised, you go according to your will; O Indra, those two bay steeds of yours [that bend the knees]. He then sprinkles three times what remains in the vessel. He worships it from that very spot with the verse, “Praised, you go according to your will; O Indra, those two bay steeds of yours [that bend the knees].”

4.4.3.2332. With the verse, "They have eaten, they have indeed rejoiced" (*akṣann amīmadanta hi*), he addresses the Gārhapatya fire: "The dear ones have shaken themselves free; the self-luminous inspired poets (*viprāḥ*) have praised with a most new hymn. Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses. 4.4.3.24.

He recites, "Together, O Bulls, mount the chariot," and thereby establishes himself upon the speech of the Āryas: "O Indra, you who have found the cattle, who have observed the full vessel as a yoking-place—now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses."
4.4.3.25. They enter [the hall] with the words, “The Soma-loving ancestors have rejoiced.

4.4.3.26. And whatever remains in the vessel, he smells at it three times with the mantra: “Those kinsmen of mine who are like-minded, living, and among the living—may their prosperity be established in me in this world for a hundred years.”

4.4.3.27. "Homage to you, O fathers, for the sake of sap; may I become a Vasiṣṭha"—with these words of homage he worships. "Homage to you, O fathers, for the sake of heat; may I become a Vasiṣṭha"—thus [he worships]. 4.4.3.28. Then he pours out three vessels of water.

4.4.3.29. With the words, “May the fathers cleanse themselves,” he [sprinkles water] on the southern hip; with “May the grandfathers cleanse themselves,” on the right shoulder; and with “May the great-grandfathers cleanse themselves,” on the left shoulder. 4.4.3.30.
He takes the eye-ointment and the ointment for the feet, saying, “May the fathers be anointed. He applies the ointment with the words, “May the fathers be anointed.”

4.4.3.31. He anoints [the feet] on the right hip with the formula: "May the fathers anoint; may the fathers anoint; may the fathers anoint; may the fathers anoint. He anoints twice and anoints once more.

4.4.3.32. "Regarding this *sūtra*, N₁ reads: ‘*abhyañjatāṃ pitāmahā iti dakṣiṇe ’ṃse ’bhyanakti; āñjatāṃ pitāmahā abhyañjatāṃ pitāmahā iti dvir abhyanakti; sakṛd ānakty āñjatāṃ pitāmahā abhyañjatāṃ pitāmahā*’. Thus, on the right shoulder, he anoints twice and anoints thoroughly once.

4.4.3.33. With the words, “May the great-grandfathers anoint themselves,” he anoints the left shoulder. He anoints twice with the words, “May the great-grandfathers smear themselves” and “May the great-grandfathers anoint themselves. He smears once.
4.4.3.34. He cuts off the fringe, saying: "O fathers, this is your garment... may he make me free from calamity" (up to sūtra 40), and "O fathers, give this hero to me.
4.4.3.35. "In the latter part of life, one should cut the hair," according to the Brāhmaṇa.
4.4.3.36. He cuts off only the fringe.
4.4.3.37. He worships with the verse, "The fathers have eaten," and continues, "The fathers have rejoiced; the fathers have been satisfied; the fathers have cleansed themselves. 4.4.3.38.
He concludes with, "Depart, O Soma-loving fathers," and, "In the deep [waters], they rejoice in the common feast. 4.4.3.39.
With the three verses beginning, "Now we summon the mind," he summons the mind, ending with, "May we be united with the living company through the Nārāśaṃsa cup."
4.4.3.40. With the verse, "That which [is in] the intermediate space, the earth, and the sky," he worships the *gārhapatya* fire from that very spot with the formula, "May [it] make me free from sin.
4.4.3.41. While they put on their sacrificial threads (*yajñopavīta*), they proceed in a straight line.
4.4.3.42. They move the southern half of the enclosing stick; they remove it. They turn around the enclosure.
4.4.3.43. Having offered the *santati* oblation, he offers the oblation of the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula.
4.4.3.44. Saying, "We shall set forth; having placed a fuel-stick on the fire, cleanse it once, cleanse it once," he performs two after-offerings (*anūyāja*) without the *barhis* grass.
4.4.3.45. Having returned, he separates the two offering-spoons with the two *vājavatī* verses.
4.4.3.46. With the *śaṃyu*-formula, he strews together the *prastara* and the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
4.4.3.47. The wife does not sit beside the fire; they do not perform the *saṃyāja* offerings. 4.4.3.48. He does not offer the *samiṣṭayajus*.

4.4.3.49. Right here, whatever remains of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), whatever remains of the roasted grains (*dhānā*), and whatever remains of the stirred drink (*mantha*)—all that they pour together. 4.4.3.50.

With the verse, “O Prajāpati, none other than you [possesses] these... (VS 11.42), he goes toward half of the Āhavanīya fire with the words, “All created beings... of riches” (VS 11.43). 4.4.3.51. The Pitṛyajña is concluded.
4.4.3.52. They scatter the Tryambaka cakes into the hollow of the treasury-vessel.
4.4.3.53. He prepares the final leaf of a Palāśa tree.
4.4.4 [Disposal of the Fire] 4.4.4.1. Prepare the final leaf of a *palāśa* tree.
4.4.4.2. They station sentinels toward these directions—the west and the north—and at the crossroads.
4.4.4.3. Taking a single firebrand from elsewhere with [the verse beginning] "The other... and a water-pot, having addressed the young girls, they go out toward the north with the *tryambaka* verses.

4.4.4.4. With the words, “As many as we are, both those who live with us and those who do not” (ŚB 1.8.6b,c), he worships the *gārhapatya* fire with the formula: “To them I have done what is pleasing; you are the shelter of cattle, the shelter of the sacrificer—grant me shelter. [cf. E280]

4.4.4.5. With the mantra, “The rat is your animal, O Rudra” (TS 1.8.6e,f), he places the Tryambaka cake upon a molehill with the formula: “Be pleased with that! This is your portion, O Rudra; together with your sister Ambikā, be pleased with it. 4.4.4.6.
Having placed a single firebrand at a crossroads, he adds fuel to it. 4.4.4.7.
From the last leaf of a Palāśa tree, he cuts off portions of the Tryambaka cakes.

4.4.4.8. Standing to the west of the fire, he recites the invitatory verse (*puro’nuvākyā*) beginning with: “*bheṣajaṃ gava*. He recites: “*Aśvāya puruṣāya bheṣajaṃ meṣyai kṛdhi*”—that is, “Prepare a remedy for the horse, for the man, and for the ram and the ewe.”

4.4.4.9. With the words, “We have appeased Rudra, O Mother” (RV 1.43.1, with variant), he sacrifices, saying: “O God Tryambaka, protect us! May he make us prosperous, may he grant us all, may he cause us to prosper, and may our entire world be free from disease and well-disposed—svāhā! Having said this, he throws [the offering] after [the fire].
4.4.4.10. He digs up the *tryambaka* fruits from the hollow of a *parṇa* leaf.
4.4.4.11. They crush them; they collect them; they place them in the joined palms of the sacrificer. 4.4.4.12–14.

Striking their right thighs, they walk around [the fire] three times to the left, reciting: “We worship Tryambaka... (RV 7.59.12)”; and [reciting]: “May I be released from what is ill-smelling, but not from what is sweet-smelling; may I be released from death, not from immortality. (RV 7.59.12).
4.4.4.13. They pull them out; they crush them; they collect them; they pour them into the joined palms of the sacrificer. 4.4.4.14.
Striking their right thighs, they walk around [the fire] by the way they came, reciting: “We worship Tryambaka,” and “Make me fragrant from immortality.”

4.4.4.15 {Not in C.}. They do not dig them up; they do not dig them up three times. They crush them; they collect them; they pour them into the very joined palms of the sacrificer. 4.4.4.16 {Not in C.}.
With the words, "We worship Tryambaka," they walk around [the altar] to the right, striking their right thighs, [with the verse] "Fragrant, beyond death.
4.4.4.17 {Not in C.}. Moving silently, striking their left thighs, they walk back along the same path.
4.4.4.1835. A maiden desiring a husband should say: "May I be released from death, not from immortality. 4.4.4.19.
They pour these [grains] into her joined palms. 4.4.4.2036.
With the words, "I unite you with fortune, as one unites *surā* with *māsara*," he then pours them into the joined palms of the sacrificer himself.

4.4.4.21 Having made those [leaves] into bundles, the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer, taking a water-pot with a carrying-pole, carry them to dry ground and hang them on a dry stump, saying: "This is your portion, O Rudra; accept it, you who are clothed in skins. 4.4.4.22 Having sprinkled water around, they return without looking back.
4.4.4.23 Having returned, he releases [the fires]: he places the former fire into the latter Āhavanīya fire.

4.4.4.24. Having set out the sacrificial implements, he should lead forward the waters and offer the *āditya* oblation of cooked rice (*caru*). 4.4.4.25. Once it has been offered, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.
4.4.4.26. When [the oblation] has been placed down, he recites the *apānagraha* formulas, the *pṛśni* verses, and the *daśahotṛ* formula.
4.4.4.27. For this [offering], the two *ājyabhāga* portions belong to Vṛtrahan.
4.4.4.28. "Recite for Aditi," he says, while spreading [the base] and cutting [the portion].
4.4.4.29. "May Aditi protect us," he recites.
4.4.4.30. He sacrifices with the verse, “O Mother Earth,” and offers the oblation when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered.
4.4.4.31. The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
4.4.4.32. He offers the oblation continuously following the oblation of the Hotṛ.

4.4.4.33. The ritual action is accomplished; this iṣṭi is concluded. 4.4.4.34. Following the conclusion, he causes the oblation to cease. 4.4.4.35. The preparatory materials are successfully prepared.

4.4.4.36. "He who turned around this great earth by means of the seasons, [measuring] the ends of the earth with his sharp flame—by the splendor of Vaiśvānara, by *ṛta*, I turn you back; by truth I turn you around; by auspiciousness I bring you near. That is *ṛta*, that is truth, that is the vow. May I be able to do that; may I be able through that."

With the formula, "I am the one to be accomplished; I am the one to be accomplished," he subsequently scatters [the earth]—first to the south, then to the west, then to the north, and then in the middle.
Following the conclusion of the oblation, he performs the sacrifice with the well-known full-moon oblation.
He performs the *devavrata* rites. [Thus ends the fourth section.]

When it is said, "Today is the full moon of Pauṣa under the asterism Mṛgaśīrṣa," having arranged the sacrificial implements and having carried forward the water, he offers the Śunāsīrya oblation: a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, a pap for Soma, a cake on twelve potsherds for Savitṛ, a pap for Sarasvatī, a pap for Pūṣan, a cake on twelve potsherds for Indra-Agni, and a pap for Viśve Devāḥ, [and] for Indra.

[He prepares] a cake on twelve potsherds for Śunāsīra, milk for Vāyu, and a cake on one potsherd for Sūrya. 4.5.1.2. Once [the grain] has been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses. 4.5.1.3. Having released his speech with the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviskṛt*), he offers the *pañcahotṛ* formula into the *āhavanīya* fire with [clarified butter] taken four times.
4.5.1.4. The sacrificial oblations are cooked. 4.5.1.5. When the oblations are cooked, he performs the *stambayajus* rite, encloses the altar (*vedi*), and mutters the *karaṇa* formula. 4.5.1.6.
Having been urged, he performs the second enclosure.

4.5.1.7. Having stirred [the grains] and having propped [the ladle], he issues the command: "Set down the sprinkling waters; place the fuel and the sacrificial grass nearby; cleanse the dipping-spoon and the offering-ladles; gird the wife [or: having girt her]; come forth with the clarified butter; bring curds for the speckled butter; come, O Sacrificer—performing that [which you have been told]."

4.5.1.7. They perform this: having wiped the *sruva* and the *sruca*s, he takes portions of clarified butter (*ājya*), including the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*). He sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass (*idhmābarhis*); he sprinkles the altar (*vedi*); he sprinkles the seat (*āsana*). 4.5.1.8. Having poured out the water, he takes the *prastara* bundle; he spreads the sacrificial grass. 4.5.1.9.
Having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*); he places two fuel-sticks (*samidh*) upon the fire.
4.5.1.10. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), he yokes the fire.

4.5.1.11. Having returned, he places the *tiraścī* [ladle] down; upon the two *tiraścī* [sticks] he places the *prastara* [bunch of grass]; upon the *prastara* the *juhū* [ladle]; and the other two [ladles, *upabhṛt* and *dhruvā*], upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
4.5.1.12. They adorn the oblations (*havis*) one after another in due order.
4.5.1.13. He removes [the sacrificial portions] after they have been spread with a base of ghee and sprinkled over with ghee.
4.5.1.14. Having sprinkled the oblations all over with ghee, they bring them forward.
4.5.1.15. When they have been set down, he recites the *apānagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.

4.5.1.16. Having touched [the fire-places] together with the mantra, “The firm ones have sat down; that which is mine, O Agni” (cf. MS 1.1.12:8.3; KS 1.11:6; VS 2.6), he recites the Pañcahotṛ formula. 4.5.1.17.
He proceeds with the fire produced by friction (nirmanthya). 4.5.1.18. He recites the invitatory verse for the fire being kindled: “To Agni, being kindled... (MS 1.1.12:8.3–4).

4.5.1.19. He recites seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses. 4.5.1.20. When the *sāmidhenīs* have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* ladle, he says: "O *Āgnīdh*, cleanse the fires thrice each! 4.5.1.21. Without letting the two *sruc* ladles touch each other, having stepped across and anointed the *dhruvā* [ladle], and having set it down, he chooses the *pravara*. He sets it down and chooses the *pravara*.
4.5.1.22. The Hotṛ sits down; being impelled, he takes up the two offering-spoons.
4.5.1.23. He performs nine fore-offerings (prayāja).
4.5.1.24. He says, “O Śrauṣaṭ! Make it heard!”—“Sacrifice the fuel-sticks (samidh)—sacrifice, sacrifice!”
4.5.1.25. Having poured half [of the butter] from the *upabhṛt* into the *dhruvā* at the fourth [offering], one pours all [the remainder] into it at the eighth.
4.5.1.26. One performs the *prayāja* offerings using all [the butter] remaining in the *upabhṛt*.

4.5.1.27. Having performed the *prayāja* offerings and stepped across, he bastes the *dhruvā* and then the oblations in successive order, ending with the clotted butter (*pṛṣadājya*), but not the *upabhṛt*; for that [ladle] remains empty.
4.5.1.28. He offers the two *ājyabhāga* (butter-portions). The two *ājyabhāgas* are the *vārtraghna* (slayers of Vṛtra). 4.5.1.29.
Saying, “Recite for Agni,” he speaks while spreading the underlayer of butter and taking the portion.
4.5.2.1. "Recite for Agni," he says, while spreading [the base of clarified butter] and cutting [the portion].
4.5.2.2. The invitatory verses (*puro'nuvākyā*) and offering verses (*yājyā*) for the seven oblations are well-known.
4.5.2.3. "Recite for Indra Śunāsīra," he says, while spreading [the base of clarified butter] and cutting [the portion].

4.5.2.4. He recites: “Indra we, Śunāsīra... [and continues] “...we invoke at this sacrifice; may he come to us with strengths, with strengths we invoke him. 4.5.2.5. With the words “Forward the oblations,” he performs the offering: “O Indra, lover of bay horses, bring together with your steeds the offerings rich in ghee for him; increasing through the prayer and the seasons, O Śunāsīra, graciously accept this oblation. 4.5.2.6. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.

4.5.2.7. He says, "Recite for Vāyu," while spreading [the base] and cutting [the portion]. 4.5.2.8. He recites the invitatory verse: "Of Vāyu, a hundred bay steeds... 4.5.2.9. He offers the oblation with the offering verse: "...with which you go forth to the donor. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the libation.
4.5.2.10. "Recite for the *śūrya*," he says, as he places the cake on one potsherd (*ekakapāla*), which has been spread with butter and sprinkled over.

4.5.2.11. He recites, "Upwards that Jātavedas... and sacrifices with, "...the bright face of the gods has risen. At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he offers the oblation. 4.5.2.12. "Recite for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt," he says, while spreading [butter] and cutting [portions].
4.5.2.13. He cuts portions from the northern half of all the oblations one by one.
4.5.2.14. Having cut a portion from the single-potsherd cake from its receptacle, he pours clarified butter over it twice; he does not re-anoint it. 4.5.2.15. He recites: "Awaken Agni with the hymn."
4.5.2.16. He offers with the mantra, "Śaḥ havyavāṭ," and pours the oblation when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 4.5.2.17.
Having stepped across and placed the two spoons in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion. 4.5.2.18. Having touched water, he cuts off the *iḍā* portion.
4.5.2.19. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places [a portion] for the *agnīdh*.
4.5.2.20. They consume [the portions], they sprinkle themselves for purification, and they carry [the remains] around.
4.5.2.21. When the *brahman* has consumed the *prāśitra* from the sacrificial porridge (*caru*), having cast the sacrificer’s share [into it], they remove the oblations from the fire.
4.5.2.22. At the *anvāhārya* [rice-offering], he causes [the sacrificer] to recite.

4.5.2.23. Following the continuity [of the offering], he performs two *viṣṭambha-anvāroha* oblations: "To the lord of the sky, svāhā!"—these are the *anvārohas*; "To the lord of heaven, svāhā!"—[these are the *anvārohas*]. 4.5.2.24.
"To the support, the lord of distress, svāhā!"—these are the *anvārohas*.
4.5.2.25. Having said, "Come, O sacrificer," while the sacrificer has taken hold [of him], he offers the third oblation for the Hotṛ.
4.5.2.26. Saying, "O Brahman, we shall proceed," he performs nine after-offerings (anūyāja) with the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya).
4.5.2.27. Having returned, he separates the two ladles (sruk) with the two Vājavatī verses.

4.5.2.28. He strews the *prastara* and the enclosing sticks with the *śaṃyu*-formula [four times]. 4.5.2.29. Having gone away and offered the *phalīkaraṇa* oblation, they cause the wives to sacrifice together. Having gone away and offered the *phalīkaraṇa* oblation, having come back toward the east, he offers three *samiṣṭayajus* oblations.

4.5.2.30. Having offered with the *sruva* ladle, saying, “O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice; go to the lord of the sacrifice—O thou of good heroes, *svāhā!*,” and having replenished the *dhruvā* vessel, he offers with the *sruc* ladle five times [with the formula] “O gods who know the way” (*devā gātuvida*), saying, “Having found the way, *svāhā*; may Vāta support it” (*gātuṃ vitvā svāhā vātadhā*). 4.5.2.31. He concludes the oblation according to the completion of the rite. 4.5.2.32. The materials for the preparation are well-known.

4.5.2.33. He bestowed one month upon the creatures from the Supreme Lord; with that he brought greatness to them, immortality to mortals. You are born again according to your offspring; that which is yours, both mortal and immortal, by which I cause the months to revolve for you so that you may live—Agni with his sharp flame, [the power] of Vaiśvānara...

"I turn you back with *ṛta*, I turn you around with *satya*, I bring you near with *śiva*. May I prosper through that *ṛta*. With this, he first shaves the hair in front, then on the right, then behind, then on the left, and then in the middle.
4.5.2.34. Following the conclusion of the oblation, he performs the sacrifice with the well-known full-moon oblation. Thus ends the fifth Anuvāka. Thus ends the fourth Prapāṭhaka.

9. O Maruts, those triple-layered shelters which you provide for the one who exerts himself and for the donor—extend them to us! Bestow upon us, O bulls, wealth accompanied by heroic sons. 10.
For King Varuṇa has made wide a path for the sun to follow; he has provided feet where there was no place for feet to be set down, and he is the remover even of that which pierces the heart.

11. O King, let there be a hundred physicians for you, a thousand! Let your benevolence be wide and deep. Drive away hatred and destruction far off; release us from whatever sin we have committed. 12. The noose of Varuṇa has been stepped upon. The face of Agni has entered the waters. The Son of the Waters, protecting his divine power, dwells in every house. O Agni, sacrifice the fuel; let your tongue rise up toward the clarified butter.
Soma has told me within the waters: "All medicines are therein—both Agni, the source of universal well-being, and the waters, which possess all healing powers."

14. O Agni, you who know, may you ward off from us the offense against the god Varuṇa. As the best of sacrificers, the most excellent bearer of oblations, and the brightly shining one, release us from all hostilities.
15. O Agni, be our protector, our closest helper at the dawning of this very morning. Being gracious, appease Varuṇa for us; grant us mercy, and be easy for us to invoke.

16. O *avabhṛtha*, you who sink down, you are the one who sinks down; with the help of the gods, you have wiped away the sin committed against the gods; with the help of mortals, you have wiped away the sin committed against mortals. O God, protect us from wide-reaching harm. 17. May the waters and the plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Varuṇa, loosen the uppermost bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one. Then, O Āditya, in your service may we be sinless before Aditi.
Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness, we have gone from among the gods to Sūrya, the god, the supreme light.
20. Mantra variant. Cf. Ṛgveda-Brāhmaṇa 1.5.5.2: That which Gharma caused to revolve—the ends of the earth and of heaven—Agni by his sovereign might, Varuṇa together with his prayers.

Indra, together with his friends the Maruts; Agni, with his sharp flame; the Uṣṇih meter has heated the head placed upon the heat. By the splendor of Vaiśvānara, by *ṛta*, I turn it back; by *satya*, I turn it around; by *tapas*, I follow it; by the auspicious, I bring it near; by the powerful, I turn it toward me.

That is the cosmic order (*ṛta*); that is the truth (*satya*). That is the vow; may I be able to fulfill it. Through that may I have power; through that may I succeed. He who, upon the skin of this earth, causes the plants to turn back—Agni, ruling with might, Varuṇa together with his prayers, Indra with his friends the Maruts, and Agni with his sharp flame—with heat and fervor, he has overcome the *uṣṇihā*.

Welcome as a guest in our home, O Agni! Come to this sacrifice of ours, you who are wise. Having struck down all assailants, bring away the provisions of those who act as enemies.
O Agni, be bold for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent. Make our lordship easy to govern; trample down the greatness of those who act as enemies.
O Soma, you are discerning through your wisdom; you lead us along the straightest path. By your guidance, O Indu, our wise ancestors obtained their share of treasure among the gods.

(2.6.12.1.c) For by you, O Soma, our ancient fathers, the wise ones, performed their sacred rites, O Pavamāna. Winning [the prize], unassailed, open up the enclosures; be a bountiful patron for us with heroes and horses! (2.6.12.2) [Be so] for us!

27. Cf. TS 2.6.12.3: Invited are the Soma-loving Fathers, seated upon the sacred grass at their dear offerings. May they come hither; may they hear us here; may they speak for us; may they protect us.

O Agniṣvātta gods, who have partaken of the parched grain (*karambha*) offered with milk, rising up—both those below and those above—in harmony with the seasons and accompanied by Indra, may you graciously accept this oblation.
29. O Agni Kavyavāhana, when you sacrifice to the Pitṛs who increase the cosmic order (*ṛtāvṛdh*), you shall carry forth the offerings both to the gods and to the Pitṛs. (TB 2.6.16.2n, *pratīka*)

[Mantra 30, variant; cf. TB 2.6.16.2 (r): Honoring Agni—the bearer of oblations, the undecaying, the much-beloved—with clarified butter as an offering, [and] Upasad, the bearer of *kavyas* for the fathers—may he provide us with offspring rich in heroes.
O Maghavan, we shall gladden you who are so beautiful to behold. Now, O you whose chariot-seat is full, being praised, you go according to our desires. Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses!
They have eaten and they have rejoiced; the dear ones have shaken themselves free. The self-luminous sages have praised you with their newest hymn. Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay steeds.
33. May those kinsmen who are of one mind, my living ones among the living, may their prosperity be ordained for me in this world for a hundred years. 34.
We sacrifice to Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity. Like a cucumber from its stalk, may I be released from death, not from immortality.

Cf. BŚS 5.16:152.2–5: Then they walk three times around this fire from left to right, striking their right thighs, [reciting]: “We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity; may I be released from death like a cucumber from its stem, but not from immortality” (TS 1.8.6.2i). Having walked around once, they stand to the north.
Desiring to obtain [the fruit], they dig it up [with the formula]: “For Bhaga, thee! (TS 1.8.6.2k).
In this very manner they proceed a second time;
in this manner a third time. Then he pours them into the joined palms of the sacrificer.

"‘I unite you with offspring, as one unites *surā* with *māsara*’—with these words, the sacrificer pours them into the joined palms of his wife. ‘I unite you with offspring and cattle, as one unites *surā* with *māsara*’—[he says].
Then the wife [pours them] for her daughter who desires fortune, saying: ‘I unite you with fortune, as one unites *surā* with *māsara*’."

37. Having placed these [offerings] in a bag and tied them with two threads, one blue and one red, he fastens them to either a dry stump or a forked branch [of a tree], saying: "This, O Rudra, is your portion; enjoy it! With this favor, go beyond the Mūjavat mountains, with your bow unstrung, the Pināka in your hand, and clad in a skin.
38. Then, having poured out the water and cast aside the vessel, they return without looking back.

40. Offer the oblations rich in clarified butter to him, the lord of the bay horses, together with his companions. O Indra, increasing through the sacred word (*brahman*) according to the seasons, O Śunāsīrī, enjoy this offering.
